at tabe.explanation: "At tabe" means "to lose" a game, a fight or a bet: Vi taber kampen (We lose the match). It can also mean "to drop" something: Jeg tabte min telefon (I dropped my phone). For losing an item you cannot find, use at miste (to lose something): Jeg har mistet min nøgle (I have lost my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **tabe** glasset på gulvet.
sentence.en: I don't want to drop the glass on the floor.

at tabe sig.explanation: "At tabe sig" means "to lose weight": Han har tabt sig ti kilo (He has lost ten kilos). Without sig, at tabe means "to drop" or "to lose": Jeg tabte min telefon (I dropped my phone).

sentence.da: Han vil **tabe sig** og spiser mere grønt.
sentence.en: He wants to lose weight and eats more vegetables.

at tage.explanation: "At tage" means "to take", and it is used in many everyday phrases: tage bussen (take the bus), tage et billede (take a picture), tage bad (take a shower). It can also mean "to go": Jeg tager til København (I am going to Copenhagen). Tag! means "Take it!" or "Here you go!".

sentence.da: Du kan **tage** en kage fra bordet.
sentence.en: You can take a cake from the table.

at tage af.explanation: "At tage af" means "to take off" clothes: Jeg tager jakken af (I take my jacket off). The little word af (off) goes after the thing you take off.

related.en: to put on, to gain weight

sentence.da: Jeg har det varmt og vil **tage af**.
sentence.en: I feel warm and want to take something off.

at tage af bordet.explanation: "At tage af bordet" means "to clear the table", taking the plates and cups away after a meal: Jeg tager af bordet efter maden (I clear the table after the meal). Af (off) says that the things come off the table.

sentence.da: Efter maden skal vi **tage af bordet**.
sentence.en: After the meal we have to clear the table.

at tage af sted.explanation: "At tage af sted" means "to set off", to leave for somewhere: Vi tager af sted klokken otte (We set off at eight). Add the place after: Vi tager af sted til Aarhus (We set off for Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage af sted** om ti minutter.
sentence.en: We have to set off in ten minutes.

at tage bad.explanation: "At tage bad" means "to take a shower" or "to take a bath": Jeg tager bad hver morgen (I take a shower every morning). For a soak in the tub, say at tage et karbad (to take a bath in the tub).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage bad** efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: I want to take a shower after the run.

at tage bussen.explanation: "At tage bussen" means "to take the bus" or "to go by bus".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage bussen** til arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to take the bus to work.

at tage det roligt.explanation: "At tage det roligt" means "to take it easy": Jeg tager det altid roligt om søndagen (I always take it easy on Sundays). As a command, Tag det roligt! can also mean "Calm down!".

sentence.da: I weekenden vil jeg **tage det roligt** hjemme.
sentence.en: On the weekend I want to take it easy at home.

at tage en beslutning.explanation: "At tage en beslutning" means "to make a decision". Danes say tage (take) a decision where English says make one: Jeg har taget en beslutning (I have made a decision).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tage en beslutning** inden fredag.
sentence.en: I have to make a decision before Friday.

at tage en uddannelse.explanation: "At tage en uddannelse" means "to get an education", to complete a program that qualifies you for a job. Danes say tage (take) here: Hun tager en uddannelse som sygeplejerske (She is training to be a nurse). It covers university and trades alike.

sentence.da: Efter gymnasiet vil han **tage en uddannelse** som elektriker.
sentence.en: After high school, he wants to train as an electrician.

at tage et billede.explanation: "At tage et billede" means "to take a picture". At tage et foto (to take a photo) means the same. To say what is in the picture, use af (of): tage et billede af maden (to take a picture of the food).

sentence.da: Må jeg **tage et billede** af dig?
sentence.en: May I take a picture of you?

at tage fat.explanation: "At tage fat" means "to grab hold" and "to get to work". Add i for a physical grip: tage fat i rebet (grab hold of the rope). Add på for taking on a task: tage fat på arbejdet (get to work on it).

forms.en: to get to work / grab hold
I get to work / grab hold
I got to work / grabbed hold
I have gotten to work / grabbed hold

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage fat** på renoveringen i morgen.
sentence.en: We have to get started on the renovation tomorrow.

at tage fejl.explanation: "At tage fejl" means "to be wrong", about an opinion or a guess: Du tager fejl (You are wrong). A mistake in a task is en fejl (a mistake): Jeg lavede en fejl (I made a mistake).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt **tage fejl**, men det tror jeg ikke.
sentence.en: I could be wrong, but I do not think so.

at tage fri.explanation: "At tage fri" means "to take time off", which you decide yourself: Jeg tager fri på fredag (I am taking Friday off). When you are allowed to leave, use at få fri (to get off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage fri** på mandag.
sentence.en: I want to take Monday off.

at tage hensyn.explanation: "At tage hensyn" means "to be considerate", or to take others into account: Du skal tage hensyn til de andre (You have to be considerate of the others). Add til (to) before who or what you consider.

sentence.da: Man skal **tage hensyn** til naboerne.
sentence.en: You have to be considerate of the neighbors.

at tage hensyn til.explanation: "At tage hensyn til" means "to take into account", or "to be considerate of": Vi tager hensyn til dem, der sover (We are considerate of those who are sleeping). Du skal tage hensyn til vejret (You have to take the weather into account).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage hensyn til** naboerne om natten.
sentence.en: We must be considerate of the neighbors at night.

at tage hjem.explanation: "At tage hjem" means "to go home", usually leaving a place such as work or a party. Normally tage means "to take", but in this phrase it means "to go".

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **tage hjem** efter arbejde.
sentence.en: We would like to go home after work.

at tage imod.explanation: "At tage imod" means "to receive / accept": Vi tager imod gæster klokken seks (We receive guests at six). For a gift or help, it means accept: Hun tog imod hjælpen (She accepted the help).

sentence.da: Han vil ikke **tage imod** penge fra os.
sentence.en: He will not accept money from us.

at tage med.explanation: "At tage med" means "to bring along" or "to come along". With a thing, it means bring: Jeg tager en jakke med (I bring a jacket along). With a person, it means join: Må jeg tage med? (May I come along?). Med (along) goes last.

sentence.da: Vil du **tage med** os i biografen?
sentence.en: Do you want to come along with us to the movies?

at tage medicin.explanation: "At tage medicin" means "to take medicine": Jeg tager min medicin hver morgen (I take my medicine every morning).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og skal **tage medicin**.
sentence.en: I am sick and have to take medicine.

at tage noter.explanation: "At tage noter" means "to take notes", putting the main points on paper while someone talks: Jeg tager noter i timen (I take notes in class).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage noter**, fordi jeg glemmer alt.
sentence.en: I want to take notes because I forget everything.

at tage op.explanation: "At tage op" means "to pick up", and also "to take up": Jeg tager bogen op fra gulvet (I pick the book up from the floor). Hun tog golf op (She took up golf).

forms.en: I have picked up / taken up

sentence.da: Det vil jeg gerne **tage op** på mødet.
sentence.en: I would like to take that up at the meeting.

at tage på.explanation: "At tage på" means "to gain weight": Jeg har taget på i julen (I gained weight over Christmas). With a trip it means something else: at tage på ferie (to go on vacation).

sentence.da: Hvis du spiser meget kage, kan du **tage på**.
sentence.en: If you eat a lot of cake, you can gain weight.

at tage på ferie.explanation: "At tage på ferie" means "to go on vacation": Vi tager på ferie i juli (We go on vacation in July). To say you are already on vacation, use at være på ferie (to be on vacation).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tage på ferie** til Spanien.
sentence.en: We want to go to Spain on vacation.

at tage sig af.explanation: "At tage sig af" means "to take care of", for people and animals: Hun tager sig af sin syge mor (She takes care of her sick mother). It also works for jobs: Jeg tager mig af opvasken (I will take care of the dishes).

sentence.da: Han vil **tage sig af** hunden i weekenden.
sentence.en: He will take care of the dog on the weekend.

at tage sig sammen.explanation: "At tage sig sammen" means "to pull oneself together", to steady yourself and make an effort, often after being lazy or upset. It is often said as an order: Nu må du tage dig sammen! (Now you must pull yourself together!)

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **tage sig sammen** og begynde at træne.
sentence.en: She wants to pull herself together and start working out.

at tage sig tid.explanation: "At tage sig tid" means "to take one's time", to do something without rushing. It is a kind thing to say to someone: Tag dig tid! (Take your time!). Add til at + verb for what you take time for: Han tager sig tid til at tænke (He takes his time to think).

sentence.da: Man kan **tage sig tid**, når der ikke er travlt.
sentence.en: You can take your time when there is no rush.

at tage skeen i den anden hånd.explanation: "At tage skeen i den anden hånd" means "to change your approach", to start doing things in a stricter and more careful way because the old way is not working. Literally it is "to take the spoon in the other hand". It is used about a person, a team or a company.

forms.da: Han tog skeen i den anden hånd
Vi må tage skeen i den anden hånd
Nu tager hun skeen i den anden hånd
forms.en: Now she is changing her approach

sentence.da: Vi bruger for mange penge og må **tage skeen i den anden hånd**.
sentence.en: We spend too much money and must change our approach.

at tage skraldet ud.explanation: "At tage skraldet ud" means "to take out the trash", carrying the household garbage outside. Ud (out) goes last, after skraldet (the trash): Jeg tager skraldet ud (I take the trash out).

forms.en: I have taken out the trash

sentence.da: Kan du **tage skraldet ud**, når du går?
sentence.en: Can you take out the trash when you leave?

at tage stilling til.explanation: "At tage stilling til" means "to take a position on", to form a clear view about something that needs an answer. It is about making up your mind: Jeg har ikke taget stilling endnu (I have not made up my mind yet).

forms.en: I have taken a position on

sentence.da: Du skal **tage stilling til** tilbuddet i dag.
sentence.en: You have to take a position on the offer today.

at tage tid.explanation: "At tage tid" means "to take time", and Danes usually start with det (it): Det tager tid at lære dansk (It takes time to learn Danish). For something slow, say det tager lang tid (it takes a long time).

sentence.da: Det vil **tage tid** at bygge et hus.
sentence.en: It will take time to build a house.

at tage toget.explanation: "At tage toget" means "to take the train" or "to go by train". The past form tog looks the same as et tog (a train), so the context tells you which is meant: Jeg tog toget (I took the train).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage toget** til København.
sentence.en: I want to take the train to Copenhagen.

at tage tyren ved hornene.explanation: "At tage tyren ved hornene" means "to take the bull by the horns", to face a difficult problem directly instead of waiting. It is often said before a hard job: Nu tager jeg tyren ved hornene og ringer til banken (Now I will take the bull by the horns and call the bank).

forms.en: She takes the bull by the horns

forms.da: Nu må vi tage tyren ved hornene
forms.en: Now we must take the bull by the horns
He took the bull by the horns

sentence.da: Hun besluttede at **tage tyren ved hornene** og tale med chefen.
sentence.en: She decided to take the bull by the horns and talk to the boss.

at tage ud.explanation: "At tage ud" means "to go out", leaving home for a meal or a trip: Vi tager ud til stranden (We go out to the beach). It also means "to take out", to remove something from inside: Jeg tager skraldet ud (I take the trash out).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tage ud** og spise i aften.
sentence.en: We want to go out and eat tonight.

at takke.explanation: "At takke" means "to thank": Jeg vil gerne takke dig (I would like to thank you). It sounds a bit more formal. In daily life, people simply say tak (thanks) or tusind tak (thank you very much).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **takke** dig for hjælpen.
sentence.en: I would like to thank you for the help.

at tale.explanation: "At tale" means "to speak": Jeg taler dansk (I speak Danish). It also fits a speech: Han taler til holdet (He speaks to the team). For casual chatting, Danes prefer at snakke (to chat, to talk). You say at tale med nogen (to speak with someone) and at tale om noget (to talk about something).

sentence.da: Kan du **tale** dansk?
sentence.en: Can you speak Danish?

at tale med.explanation: "At tale med" means "to talk to" or "to talk with" someone. The little word med (with) comes after it: tale med nogen (to talk to someone). Kan jeg tale med Anna? means "Can I speak to Anna?".

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tale med** dig.
sentence.en: I would like to talk to you.

at tale med store bogstaver.explanation: "At tale med store bogstaver" means "to speak bluntly". Literally it is to speak with big letters. You use it when you say something so plainly that nobody can misunderstand it.

forms.da: Nu taler vi med store bogstaver
Jeg må tale med store bogstaver

sentence.da: Når han ikke forstår hints, må jeg **tale med store bogstaver**.
sentence.en: When he does not get hints, I have to speak bluntly.

at tale om.explanation: "At tale om" means "to talk about" a topic: Vi taler om fodbold (We talk about soccer). In a question, om stays at the end: Hvad taler I om? (What are you talking about?)

sentence.da: Vi vil **tale om** vejret i dag.
sentence.en: We want to talk about the weather today.

at tale sammen.explanation: "At tale sammen" means "to talk (with each other)", so it needs two or more people: Vi taler sammen hver dag (We talk to each other every day). To name the other person, use at tale med (to talk with): Jeg taler med min mor (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tale sammen** om det i morgen.
sentence.en: We need to talk about it tomorrow.

at tale sandt.explanation: "At tale sandt" means "to tell the truth": Han taler altid sandt (He always tells the truth). More often, Danes say at sige sandheden (to tell the truth): Jeg sagde sandheden (I told the truth).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **tale sandt**, også når det er svært.
sentence.en: I will always tell the truth, even when it is hard.

at tale ud.explanation: "At tale ud" means "to talk things through", to say everything that bothers you until the matter is settled. Ud adds the idea of finishing completely: Lad mig tale ud! (Let me finish speaking!)

sentence.da: Efter skænderiet ville parret **tale ud** og blive gode venner igen.
sentence.en: After the argument, the couple wanted to talk it through and be good friends again.

at tale udenom.explanation: "At tale udenom" means "to beat around the bush", to avoid the real point. Udenom means around the outside, so the picture is circling the topic and never reaching it: Tal ikke udenom! (Do not beat around the bush!) Do not mix it up with tale ud (to talk things through).

forms.en: You are beating around the bush

forms.da: Hold op med at tale udenom

forms.en: He beat around the bush the whole time

sentence.da: Hun bliver ved med at **tale udenom**, når jeg spørger om pengene.
sentence.en: She keeps beating around the bush when I ask about the money.

at tanke.explanation: "At tanke" means "to refuel", to fill a car with fuel: Jeg tanker bilen (I fill up the car). For an electric car, use at lade (to charge): Jeg lader bilen (I charge the car).

sentence.da: Bilen er næsten tom, og jeg skal **tanke**.
sentence.en: The car is almost empty, and I have to refuel.

at taste.explanation: "At taste" means "to type" or "to enter" numbers and letters by tapping buttons on a device: Jeg taster telefonnummeret (I enter the phone number). For writing text, use at skrive (to write): Jeg skriver et brev (I write a letter).

sentence.da: Du skal **taste** din pinkode og trykke OK.
sentence.en: You have to enter your PIN and press OK.

at tegne.explanation: "At tegne" means "to draw" with a pencil or pen: Han tegner en hund (He draws a dog). For painting, use at male (to paint): Hun maler et billede (She paints a picture).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tegne** et hus med en blyant.
sentence.en: I want to draw a house with a pencil.

at teste.explanation: "At teste" means "to test", finding out whether something works or how good someone is: Vi tester den nye bil (We are testing the new car). For a student, a test is often en prøve (a test or exam).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **teste** os i matematik i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher will test us in math tomorrow.

at tigge.explanation: "At tigge" means "to beg", to ask for money or food because you have nothing, or to ask again and again for something you want: Børnene tigger om slik (The children beg for candy). The thing you want comes after om.

sentence.da: Han måtte **tigge** om mad, fordi han ingenting havde.
sentence.en: He had to beg for food because he had nothing.

at tilbagebetale.explanation: "At tilbagebetale" means "to pay back", to return money. Everyday speech prefers at betale tilbage: Jeg betaler dig tilbage i morgen (I will pay you back tomorrow). The one-word form sounds more formal and fits banks and shops: Butikken tilbagebetaler beløbet (The store pays the amount back).

sentence.da: Du skal **tilbagebetale** hele lånet inden for fem år.
sentence.en: You must pay back the whole loan within five years.

at tilbagekalde.explanation: "At tilbagekalde" means "to recall" or "to revoke", to take back something that was given or sold. A company can take back a faulty product, and an authority can cancel a permit. It is built from tilbage (back) and kalde (call).

sentence.da: Firmaet måtte **tilbagekalde** bilerne, fordi bremserne ikke virkede.
sentence.en: The company had to recall the cars because the brakes did not work.

at tilbagevise.explanation: "At tilbagevise" means "to refute", to say that a claim or an accusation is false and give reasons why. It is built from tilbage (back) and vise (show), and it is stronger than just saying no.

sentence.da: Hun vil **tilbagevise** beskyldningen, fordi den ikke er sand.
sentence.en: She will refute the accusation because it is not true.

at tilbede.explanation: "At tilbede" means "to worship", to show deep respect to a higher power in prayer. It also describes loving a person almost without limit: Fansene tilbeder hende (The fans adore her).

sentence.da: I kirken kan man **tilbede** Gud sammen med andre.
sentence.en: In church, people can worship God together.

at tilberede.explanation: "At tilberede" means "to prepare" food, to turn raw ingredients into a meal by cooking: Jeg tilbereder middagen (I prepare dinner). It is mostly used for food. For getting ready for something else, use at forberede (to get ready): Jeg forbereder mig til eksamen (I am preparing for the exam).

sentence.da: Kokken vil **tilberede** fisken i ovnen og servere den.
sentence.en: The chef will prepare the fish in the oven and serve it.

at tilbringe.explanation: "At tilbringe" means "to spend (time)": Vi tilbringer weekenden hos mormor (We spend the weekend at Grandma's). It is only for time. For money, say at bruge (to spend): Jeg bruger 100 kroner (I spend 100 kroner).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tilbringe** sommeren i Jylland.
sentence.en: We want to spend the summer in Jutland.

at tilbyde.explanation: "At tilbyde" means "to offer", to hold something out for someone to accept, such as food, help or a job. The person comes first, then the thing: Jeg tilbyder dig kaffe (I offer you coffee).

sentence.da: Må jeg **tilbyde** dig en kop te?
sentence.en: May I offer you a cup of tea?

at tildele.explanation: "At tildele" means "to assign" or "to award": someone in charge decides who receives a task, a prize, or a share of something. The decision is official, so it fits schools, boards, and authorities.

sentence.da: Skolen vil **tildele** prisen til den bedste elev.
sentence.en: The school will award the prize to the best student.

at tilføje.explanation: "At tilføje" means "to add", to put something extra with what is already there: Tilføj mælk (Add milk). For numbers, say at lægge sammen (to add up).

sentence.da: Du kan **tilføje** lidt salt til suppen.
sentence.en: You can add a little salt to the soup.

at tilgive.explanation: "At tilgive" means "to forgive", to stop being angry at someone for what they did. The person comes first, then the thing: Hun tilgav ham alt (She forgave him everything).

sentence.da: Hun vil **tilgive** ham, når han siger undskyld.
sentence.en: She will forgive him when he says sorry.

at tilhøre.explanation: "At tilhøre" means "to belong to". It says who has something or which group a person is in, and the one who has it follows right after with no extra word: Huset tilhører staten (The house belongs to the state).

sentence.da: En bog kan **tilhøre** biblioteket eller en privat person.
sentence.en: A book can belong to the library or to a private person.

at tilintetgøre.explanation: "At tilintetgøre" means "to annihilate", to ruin something so completely that nothing is left. It is built from til intet (to nothing) and gøre (make), so it is literally to make into nothing.

sentence.da: Branden kunne **tilintetgøre** hele skoven på en nat.
sentence.en: The fire could annihilate the whole forest in one night.

at tilkalde.explanation: "At tilkalde" means "to summon" or "to call in", to ask someone to come right away because you need them, such as a doctor or the police. The til- adds the idea of the person coming toward you.

sentence.da: Hvis det brænder, skal du **tilkalde** brandvæsenet med det samme.
sentence.en: If there is a fire, you must call in the fire department right away.

at tillade.explanation: "At tillade" means "to allow": Min mor tillader det ikke (My mother does not allow it). In everyday speech, Danes often use at have lov til (to be allowed to): Jeg har lov til at gå (I am allowed to go).

sentence.da: Reglerne vil ikke **tillade** hunde i butikken.
sentence.en: The rules will not allow dogs in the store.

at tilmelde sig.explanation: "At tilmelde sig" means "to sign up", for a course, a team or an event: Jeg tilmelder mig et dansekursus (I sign up for a dance class). The sig changes with who signs up: Hun tilmelder sig (She signs up), Vi tilmelder os (We sign up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **tilmelde sig** inden fredag.
sentence.en: Everyone has to sign up before Friday.

at tilpasse.explanation: "At tilpasse" means "to adapt": you change something so that it suits a person or a situation, like a plan or a recipe. To change yourself instead, add sig (oneself): at tilpasse sig.

sentence.da: Vi skal **tilpasse** planen, så den passer til alle.
sentence.en: We must adapt the plan so it suits everyone.

at tilpasse sig.explanation: "At tilpasse sig" means "to adapt": you or a group learn to live with new conditions, such as a new country or a new job. Sig (oneself) turns the action back on the person doing it: Hun tilpasser sig hurtigt (She adapts quickly). Without sig, at tilpasse changes a thing, like a plan.

sentence.da: Det er svært at **tilpasse sig**, når man flytter til et nyt land.
sentence.en: It is hard to adapt when you move to a new country.

at tilsidesætte.explanation: "At tilsidesætte" means "to disregard" or "to override", to push a rule, a need or an opinion aside as if it did not matter. It is built from til side (to the side) and sætte (put).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke bare **tilsidesætte** reglerne, fordi du har travlt.
sentence.en: You cannot just disregard the rules because you are busy.

at tilskynde.explanation: "At tilskynde" means "to encourage", to move someone to do something, often with a reason or a reward. You say who and what for: tilskynde nogen til at gøre noget (to encourage someone to do something).

sentence.da: Lærerne vil **tilskynde** eleverne til at læse mere.
sentence.en: The teachers want to encourage the students to read more.

at tilstræbe.explanation: "At tilstræbe" means "to strive for", to work toward a goal and try hard to reach it. It takes the goal directly, with no small word after it: tilstræbe fred (to strive for peace).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **tilstræbe** en bedre kvalitet i år.
sentence.en: The company will strive for better quality this year.

at tilstå.explanation: "At tilstå" means "to confess", to say openly that you did something wrong or illegal, especially to the police or in court. You can use it alone, Han tilstod (He confessed), or add the deed: Han tilstod tyveriet (He confessed to the theft).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **tilstå**, fordi politiet har fundet billederne.
sentence.en: The thief will confess because the police have found the pictures.

at tiltrække.explanation: "At tiltrække" means "to attract": to draw people or things toward something. It is used for crowds, customers, and workers, and also for forces: Magneten tiltrækker jern (The magnet attracts iron).

sentence.da: Den nye park kan **tiltrække** mange turister om sommeren.
sentence.en: The new park can attract many tourists in the summer.

at tisse.explanation: "At tisse" means "to pee". It is an informal, everyday word used by children, and by adults among friends and family: Jeg skal tisse (I need to pee). In a polite setting, say Jeg skal på toilettet (I need to go to the toilet).

sentence.da: Barnet skal **tisse** på toilettet.
sentence.en: The child has to pee in the toilet.

at tjekke.explanation: "At tjekke" means "to check": Jeg tjekker tiden (I check the time). For a careful check, use at kontrollere (to check carefully); at undersøge (to examine) is for looking into something more deeply.

sentence.da: Han vil **tjekke** dækkene før turen.
sentence.en: He wants to check the tires before the trip.

at tjene.explanation: "At tjene" means "to earn", getting money for work: Jeg tjener 300 kroner i timen (I earn 300 kroner an hour). It also means "to serve", being useful for something: Det tjener et formål (It serves a purpose).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tjene** flere penge.
sentence.en: I would like to earn more money.

at tjene penge.explanation: "At tjene penge" means "to earn money" by working: Hun tjener mange penge (She earns a lot of money). To spend money, say at bruge penge (to spend money).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tjene penge** i sommerferien.
sentence.en: I want to earn money during the summer vacation.

at tolerere.explanation: "At tolerere" means "to tolerate": you let something happen, even if you dislike it, and do not try to stop it. It is used for rules, behavior, and opinions: Skolen tolererer ikke mobning (The school does not tolerate bullying). For what your body can stand, use at tåle (to stand): Jeg tåler ikke mælk (I cannot handle milk).

sentence.da: Man skal **tolerere** andres meninger, også når man er uenig.
sentence.en: You must tolerate other people's opinions, even when you disagree.

at tordne.explanation: "At tordne" means "to thunder" and is only used for the weather, with det (it) in front. The sound is en torden (thunder), and a storm with it is et tordenvejr.

sentence.da: Det begynder at **tordne**, og himlen bliver helt mørk.
sentence.en: It starts to thunder, and the sky gets completely dark.

at trampe.explanation: "At trampe" means "to stomp": you put your feet down hard and heavily, often from anger. Add på (on) and it means to flatten something underfoot: Børnene trampede på blomsterne (The children trampled the flowers).

sentence.da: Den vrede dreng begynder at **trampe** i gulvet.
sentence.en: The angry boy starts to stomp on the floor.

at transportere.explanation: "At transportere" means "to transport": to carry goods or people from one place to another, mostly over a distance and with a truck, a boat, or a plane. It is used most for goods and cargo. For people, Danes usually say at køre (to drive): Jeg kører dig hjem (I will drive you home).

sentence.da: Lastbilen skal **transportere** frugt fra Spanien til Danmark.
sentence.en: The truck must transport fruit from Spain to Denmark.

at trives.explanation: "At trives" means "to thrive": to feel happy and do well in a place, a job, or a group. It is mostly about people: Jeg trives i Aarhus (I feel at home in Aarhus). Plants thrive too: Planten trives i skygge (The plant thrives in shade).

sentence.da: Han kan **trives** i en lille by, fordi alle kender hinanden.
sentence.en: He can thrive in a small town because everyone knows each other.

at tro.explanation: "At tro" means "to believe" or "to think something is probably true": Jeg tror, det er rigtigt (I think it is right). It is also used for faith: at tro på Gud (to believe in God). For your own taste, use at synes (to think): Jeg synes, det er godt (I think it is good).

related.en: to think / to be of the opinion

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **tro** det!
sentence.en: I can't believe it!

at tro på.explanation: "At tro på" means "to believe in" something or someone: Jeg tror på dig (I believe in you). Without på, at tro means "to think": Jeg tror, det regner (I think it is raining).

sentence.da: Børn vil gerne **tro på** julemanden.
sentence.en: Children like to believe in Santa Claus.

at trodse.explanation: "At trodse" means "to defy", to refuse to follow an order or to stand up to something dangerous. It also fits things that hold up against force: Huset trodsede stormen (The house held up against the storm).

sentence.da: Hun vil **trodse** forbuddet og tage derhen alligevel.
sentence.en: She will defy the ban and go there anyway.

at true.explanation: "At true" means "to threaten": to say or show that something bad may happen. What may happen comes after med (with): Han truer med at sige op (He threatens to quit). It works for people and for dangers, as in Det truer med regn (It looks like rain).

sentence.da: Naboen kan **true** med at ringe til politiet.
sentence.en: The neighbor can threaten to call the police.

at trykke.explanation: "At trykke" means "to press" and also "to print": Jeg trykker på knappen (I press the button). For books and posters, it means printing: Vi trykker bogen (We print the book).

sentence.da: Du skal **trykke** på den grønne knap.
sentence.en: You have to press the green button.

at træde.explanation: "At træde" means "to step", putting your foot down somewhere. It usually takes a small word after it, such as ind (in) or ud (out): Han trådte ind i huset (He stepped into the house).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **træde** på blomsterne.
sentence.en: You must not step on the flowers.

at træde i kraft.explanation: "At træde i kraft" means "to take effect", used for laws, rules and agreements that start on a set date. Literally it is to step into force.

sentence.da: Loven skal **træde i kraft** den første januar.
sentence.en: The law must take effect on the first of January.

at træde tilbage.explanation: "At træde tilbage" means "to step down": to give up an important position, such as a minister, a chair, or a coach. For an ordinary job, Danes say at sige op (to quit).

sentence.da: Ministeren vil **træde tilbage**, fordi hun har mistet støtten.
sentence.en: The minister will step down because she has lost support.

at træffe.explanation: "At træffe" means "to meet" and "to make (a decision)". For people, it means to run into someone or to reach them at a place: Jeg traf Anna i byen (I ran into Anna in town). For choices, it goes with a decision or an agreement: at træffe en aftale (to make an agreement).

sentence.da: Du kan **træffe** mig på kontoret efter klokken tre.
sentence.en: You can reach me at the office after three o'clock.

at træffe en beslutning.explanation: "At træffe en beslutning" means "to make a decision". The verb træffe (to make) goes with beslutning (decision), and at lave en beslutning is not used. At tage en beslutning (to take a decision) is also common.

sentence.da: Når vi er uenige, skal chefen **træffe en beslutning**.
sentence.en: When we disagree, the boss must make a decision.

at trække.explanation: "At trække" means "to pull", moving something toward yourself, the opposite of pushing. It is also part of the phrase trække vejret (to breathe): Han trækker vejret dybt (He breathes deeply).

sentence.da: Vi må **trække** i rebet sammen.
sentence.en: We have to pull on the rope together.

at trække fra.explanation: "At trække fra" means "to subtract": Jeg trækker to fra fem (I subtract two from five). It also means to deduct an amount: Man kan trække det fra i skat (You can deduct it on your taxes).

sentence.da: Du skal **trække fra** og ikke lægge sammen.
sentence.en: You have to subtract and not add.

at trække på skuldrene.explanation: "At trække på skuldrene" means "to shrug": you lift your shoulders to show that you do not know or do not care. The Danish is built word for word from trække (to pull), på (on), and skuldrene (the shoulders).

sentence.da: Når jeg spørger hvorfor, plejer hun at **trække på skuldrene**.
sentence.en: When I ask why, she usually shrugs.

at trække sig.explanation: "At trække sig" means "to withdraw": you pull yourself out of something, such as a race, a deal, or a team. Add fra (from) for what you pull out of: Hun trak sig fra valget (She withdrew from the election). It is also what an army does when it falls back.

sentence.da: Han vil **trække sig** fra aftalen, fordi prisen er for høj.
sentence.en: He wants to withdraw from the deal because the price is too high.

at trække vejret.explanation: "At trække vejret" means "to breathe". Literally it is to pull the breath, with vejret meaning "the breath". The same word vejret also means "the weather": Vejret er flot i dag (The weather is nice today).

sentence.da: Du skal **trække vejret** dybt.
sentence.en: You must breathe deeply.

at træne.explanation: "At træne" means "to work out" or "to train": Jeg træner hver dag (I work out every day). It also means "to practice" a skill: træne dansk (to practice Danish).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **træne** tre gange om ugen.
sentence.en: I want to work out three times a week.

at trænge.explanation: "At trænge" means "to push through" and "to need": you force a way in or out, as in Vandet trænger ind (The water gets in). With til (for), it means to need, and it sounds stronger than a wish: Jeg trænger til ferie (I really need a vacation).

sentence.da: Lyset kan **trænge** ind gennem de tynde gardiner.
sentence.en: The light can get in through the thin curtains.

at trøste.explanation: "At trøste" means "to comfort": you help someone who is sad or hurt, with kind words, a hug, or just by staying close. Add med (with) for how you do it: trøste med et kram (comfort with a hug).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **trøste** min ven, fordi han har mistet sit job.
sentence.en: I want to comfort my friend because he has lost his job.

at tude.explanation: "At tude" means "to cry" in a loud, noisy way, like bawling. It is a casual word that fits a child or a close friend: Hold op med at tude! (Stop bawling!) It also means "to howl", for the long loud sound of a siren or a ship's horn.

sentence.da: Barnet begyndte at **tude**, da ballonen sprang.
sentence.en: The child started to bawl when the balloon popped.

at tvinge.explanation: "At tvinge" means "to force". To say what someone is forced to do, add til at (to): Hun tvang ham til at spise (She forced him to eat).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **tvinge** mig til at komme.
sentence.en: You cannot force me to come.

at tvivle.explanation: "At tvivle" means "to doubt", usually with på (on): Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer (I doubt that he is coming).

sentence.da: Hun begynder at **tvivle** på sig selv.
sentence.en: She is starting to doubt herself.

at tvivle på.explanation: "At tvivle på" means "to doubt": Jeg tvivler på det (I doubt it). The thing you doubt comes after på: Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer (I doubt that he is coming).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **tvivle på** mig.
sentence.en: Do not doubt me.

at tyde.explanation: "At tyde" means "to interpret", to work out what something unclear means, such as old writing or a look on a face. Do not mix it up with at tyde på (to suggest), where the facts themselves are the clue.

sentence.da: Jeg kan næsten ikke **tyde** hans håndskrift.
sentence.en: I can hardly interpret his handwriting.

at tyde på.explanation: "At tyde på" means "to suggest" or "to indicate", used when facts lead toward a conclusion. Danes often say alt tyder på, at (everything suggests that), followed by the conclusion.

sentence.da: Alle de mørke skyer kan **tyde på** regn.
sentence.en: All the dark clouds can suggest rain.

at tygge.explanation: "At tygge" means "to chew": Hunden tygger på en pind (The dog chews on a stick). The word tyggegummi (chewing gum) is built from tygge (chew) and gummi (rubber).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **tygge**, fordi min tand gør ondt.
sentence.en: I cannot chew because my tooth hurts.

at tåle.explanation: "At tåle" means "to stand" and "to tolerate": what your body, a material, or a person can take without harm. It is mostly used with ikke (not): Jeg tåler ikke larm (I cannot stand noise). It works for things too: Tøjet tåler vask (The clothes can take washing).

sentence.da: Min mave kan ikke **tåle** stærk mad.
sentence.en: My stomach cannot handle spicy food.

at tælle.explanation: "At tælle" means "to count": Jeg tæller til ti (I count to ten). Its past forms jeg talte and "jeg har talt" are exactly the same as for at tale (to speak), so the context tells you which is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg kan **tælle** til ti.
sentence.en: I can count to ten.

at tænde.explanation: "At tænde" means "to turn on" a light and also "to light" a candle, a fire or a cigarette: Tænd lyset (Turn on the light). For a TV, a radio or running water, Danes usually say tænde for (turn on) instead. Do not mix it up with at tænke (to think), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tænde** lyset i mørket.
sentence.en: I want to turn on the light in the dark.

at tænde for.explanation: "At tænde for" means "to turn on" something that runs or plays, such as the TV, the radio, the water or the heating. For a light, a candle or a fire, use tænde (to turn on, to light): tænde lyset (turn on the light).

sentence.da: Jeg fryser og vil **tænde for** varmen.
sentence.en: I am cold and want to turn on the heating.

at tænke.explanation: "At tænke" means "to think" in the sense of using your mind: Jeg tænker på dig (I am thinking of you). It goes with på (about). It is not the word for giving an opinion, which is at synes (to think, to have an opinion).

sentence.da: Lad mig **tænke** lidt.
sentence.en: Let me think a little.

at tænke over.explanation: "At tænke over" means "to think about", in the sense of thinking something over carefully: Jeg skal tænke over det (I need to think it over). To have someone in your mind, use at tænke på (to think of): Jeg tænker på dig (I am thinking of you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tænke over** dit tilbud.
sentence.en: I would like to think about your offer.

at tænke på.explanation: "At tænke på" means "to think of", for having someone or something in your mind: Jeg tænker på dig (I am thinking of you). To think something over carefully, use at tænke over (to think about): Jeg tænker over det (I am thinking it over).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke holde op med at **tænke på** ferien.
sentence.en: I cannot stop thinking about the vacation.

at tænke sig om.explanation: "At tænke sig om" means "to think carefully" before you act or answer: Tænk dig om! (Think carefully!). The small word changes with who is thinking: jeg tænker mig om (I think carefully), han tænker sig om (he thinks carefully).

sentence.da: Man bør **tænke sig om**, før man svarer.
sentence.en: You should think carefully before you answer.

at tø.explanation: "At tø" means "to thaw", when ice and snow turn to water as the weather gets warmer. It is about the weather, so it goes with det: Det tør (It is thawing). Careful: tør also means "dry", and jeg tør means "I dare".

sentence.da: Når det begynder at **tø**, bliver sneen til vand.
sentence.en: When it starts to thaw, the snow turns to water.

at tømme.explanation: "At tømme" means "to empty": Jeg tømmer skraldespanden (I empty the trash can). It takes everything out of something, so a full thing becomes tom (empty).

sentence.da: Kan du **tømme** opvaskemaskinen for mig?
sentence.en: Can you empty the dishwasher for me?

at tørre.explanation: "At tørre" means "to dry", when something loses its water, and also "to wipe", rubbing a surface clean and dry: Jeg tørrer bordet af (I wipe the table off).

sentence.da: Håndklæderne skal **tørre** i solen.
sentence.en: The towels have to dry in the sun.

at tørre af.explanation: "At tørre af" means "to wipe", for a table or shelf, and also "to dry dishes": Han tørrer bordet af (He wipes the table), Hun tørrer tallerkenerne af (She dries the plates). To mop up a spill, use at tørre op (to wipe up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tørre af** efter middagen.
sentence.en: I have to dry the dishes after dinner.

at tørre støv af.explanation: "At tørre støv af" means "to dust", wiping dust off shelves and tables: Jeg tørrer støv af på hylden (I dust the shelf). The word af stays at the end: Han tørrer støv af hver uge (He dusts every week).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tørre støv af** på hylderne i dag.
sentence.en: I have to dust the shelves today.

en t-shirt.explanation: "En t-shirt" means "a t-shirt". To say you are wearing one, use have ... på (literally have ... on): Jeg har en t-shirt på (I am wearing a t-shirt).

sentence.da: Om sommeren går jeg i **t-shirt** og shorts.
sentence.en: In the summer I wear a t-shirt and shorts.

en tabel.explanation: "En tabel" means "a table" of rows and columns with information, not a piece of furniture. For furniture, use et bord (a table).

sentence.da: Tallene står i en **tabel** på side tre.
sentence.en: The numbers are in a table on page three.

en tablet.explanation: "En tablet" means "a tablet", a flat touchscreen computer. It also means a pill: Jeg tager en tablet mod smerter (I take a pill for pain).

sentence.da: Jeg læser nyheder på min **tablet** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I read the news on my tablet every morning.

en tagrende.explanation: "En tagrende" means "a gutter", the channel along the edge of a roof that carries rainwater away.

sentence.da: Regnvand løber ned i en **tagrende**.
sentence.en: Rainwater runs down into a gutter.

en tagterrasse.explanation: "En tagterrasse" means "a roof terrace", an outdoor area on the flat roof of a building.

sentence.da: Fra vores **tagterrasse** kan vi se hele byen.
sentence.en: From our roof terrace we can see the whole city.

en taktik.explanation: "En taktik" means "a tactic", the way you act in one moment or situation to reach a goal, such as in a game or a negotiation. A strategi (strategy) is the bigger plan behind it.

sentence.da: Holdets **taktik** er at forsvare sig og vente på en chance.
sentence.en: The team's tactic is to defend and wait for a chance.

en talemåde.explanation: "En talemåde" means "a saying", a set wording whose meaning is often not the literal one, such as at tage benene på nakken (to run away fast, literally "to take the legs on the neck").

sentence.da: Man skal ikke tage hver **talemåde** helt bogstaveligt.
sentence.en: You should not take every saying completely literally.

en tallerken.explanation: "En tallerken" means "a plate", the flat dish you eat from. A deep plate for soup is en dyb tallerken (a deep plate).

sentence.da: Der er mad på min **tallerken**.
sentence.en: There is food on my plate.

en talsperson.explanation: "En talsperson" means "a spokesperson", someone chosen to speak for a group or an organization. The older word is talsmand (spokesman), and talsperson works for anyone.

sentence.da: Virksomhedens **talsperson** svarede på journalisternes spørgsmål i går.
sentence.en: The company's spokesperson answered the journalists' questions yesterday.

en tand.explanation: "En tand" means "a tooth". You say at børste tænder (to brush teeth). En tandlæge (a dentist) is literally a tooth doctor.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i en **tand** i dag.
sentence.en: One of my teeth hurts today.

en tandbøjle.explanation: "En tandbøjle" means "a brace (teeth)", wires and small brackets that slowly move the teeth into a straighter position.

sentence.da: Min datter skal have **tandbøjle**, fordi hendes tænder står skævt.
sentence.en: My daughter needs braces because her teeth are crooked.

en tandbørste.explanation: "En tandbørste" means "a toothbrush". It is built from tand (tooth) and børste (brush). Tand also starts en tandlæge (a dentist) and en tandpine (a toothache).

sentence.da: Jeg børster tænder med en **tandbørste**.
sentence.en: I brush my teeth with a toothbrush.

en tandlæge.explanation: "En tandlæge" means "a dentist", made from tand (tooth) and læge (doctor). You say Jeg skal til tandlægen (I am going to the dentist) and Jeg skal til lægen (I am going to the doctor).

sentence.da: Min **tandlæge** kigger på mine tænder.
sentence.en: My dentist looks at my teeth.

en tandlægetid.explanation: "En tandlægetid" means "a dentist appointment", built from tandlæge (dentist) and tid (appointment). Tid means both time and appointment: Jeg har ikke tid (I have no time) but Jeg har en tid klokken ti (I have an appointment at ten).

sentence.da: Til min **tandlægetid** kigger tandlægen på mine tænder.
sentence.en: At my dentist appointment, the dentist looks at my teeth.

en tandplejer.explanation: "En tandplejer" means "a dental hygienist", someone who cleans your teeth and shows you how to care for them.

sentence.da: Min **tandplejer** renser mine tænder to gange om året.
sentence.en: My dental hygienist cleans my teeth twice a year.

en tang.explanation: "En tang" means "a pair of pliers", a hand tool with two arms for gripping or cutting. It also means seaweed, the plant that washes up on the beach, and then it is not used in the plural.

sentence.da: Jeg kan klippe ledningen over med en **tang**.
sentence.en: I can cut the wire in two with pliers.

en tank.explanation: "En tank" means "a tank", especially the fuel tank of a car. It is also the word for the army vehicle.

sentence.da: Vi fylder benzin på bilens **tank**.
sentence.en: We put gas in the car's tank.

en tanke.explanation: "En tanke" means "a thought", something you think. The phrase at gøre sig tanker om noget (to think about something or worry about it) is common.

sentence.da: Når jeg tænker, kommer der en **tanke**.
sentence.en: When I think, a thought comes.

en tankstation.explanation: "En tankstation" means "a gas station". It is built from at tanke (to fill up) and station. You can use at tanke on its own: Jeg skal lige tanke (I just need to fill up the car).

sentence.da: Tanken er tom, og vi leder efter en **tankstation**.
sentence.en: The tank is empty, and we are looking for a gas station.

en tante.explanation: "En tante" means "an aunt", the sister of a parent or the wife of an uncle. More exactly, en faster (father's sister) and en moster (mother's sister) exist, but tante works for both.

sentence.da: Min **tante** er min mors søster.
sentence.en: My aunt is my mother's sister.

en tarm.explanation: "En tarm" means "an intestine", the long tube in the body where food is broken down and nutrients are absorbed.

sentence.da: En voksens **tarm** er flere meter lang og ligger i maven.
sentence.en: An adult's intestine is several meters long and lies in the belly.

en tartelet.explanation: "En tartelet" means "a tartlet (vol-au-vent)", a small, round shell of puff pastry with a hot filling. In Denmark it is often served at family parties.

sentence.da: Hun fyldte hver **tartelet** med høns og asparges.
sentence.en: She filled each tartlet with chicken and asparagus.

en taske.explanation: "En taske" means "a bag" with a handle or strap. A thin plastic shop bag is en pose (a plastic bag) instead. Words can go in front: en håndtaske (a handbag), en skoletaske (a school bag).

sentence.da: Jeg har bøger i min **taske**.
sentence.en: I have books in my bag.

en tatovering.explanation: "En tatovering" means "a tattoo", a picture or text drawn into the skin with ink. Many Danes also say en tattoo, using the English word.

sentence.da: Hun har en **tatovering** af en rose på armen.
sentence.en: She has a tattoo of a rose on her arm.

en tavle.explanation: "En tavle" means "a blackboard", the board at the front of a classroom. Add a word in front for other boards: en opslagstavle (a bulletin board).

sentence.da: Der hænger en stor **tavle** i klasseværelset.
sentence.en: A big blackboard hangs in the classroom.

en tavshed.explanation: "En tavshed" means "a silence", the quiet when nobody speaks, often a heavy or awkward one. For plain quiet with no sound at all, use stilhed (stillness).

sentence.da: Der var en lang **tavshed**, fordi ingen turde sige noget.
sentence.en: There was a long silence because nobody dared to say anything.

en taxa.explanation: "En taxa" means "a taxi". You say med taxa (by taxi) and at bestille en taxa (to book a taxi).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **taxa** til lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We take a taxi to the airport.

en taxachauffør.explanation: "En taxachauffør" means "a taxi driver", built from taxa (taxi) and chauffør (driver). You can tell the driver where to go with Til banegården, tak (To the railway station, please).

sentence.da: En **taxachauffør** kører folk rundt i byen.
sentence.en: A taxi driver drives people around the city.

en teenager.explanation: "En teenager" means "a teenager", someone between 13 and 19. The word comes from English and is used for both boys and girls.

sentence.da: Min søn er **teenager** og sover længe.
sentence.en: My son is a teenager and sleeps late.

en tegnebog.explanation: "En tegnebog" means "a wallet", the kind that holds banknotes and cards. It is the older, more formal word. In everyday speech people say en pung (a wallet): Har du din pung? (Do you have your wallet?)

sentence.da: Jeg har penge og kort i min **tegnebog**.
sentence.en: I have money and cards in my wallet.

en tegnefilm.explanation: "En tegnefilm" means "a cartoon", an animated film. Do not mix it up with en tegneserie (a comic you read on paper).

sentence.da: I en **tegnefilm** er alle figurerne tegnet.
sentence.en: In a cartoon, all the characters are drawn.

en tegner.explanation: "En tegner" means "an illustrator" or "a cartoonist", a person who draws for a living, for example for children's books or newspapers.

sentence.da: En **tegner** laver billederne til bogen, og forfatteren skriver teksten.
sentence.en: An illustrator makes the pictures for the book and the author writes the text.

en tegneserie.explanation: "En tegneserie" means "a comic" or "a comic strip". A film version is en tegnefilm (a cartoon).

sentence.da: En **tegneserie** har billeder og små talebobler.
sentence.en: A comic has pictures and small speech bubbles.

en tegning.explanation: "En tegning" means "a drawing", a picture made with a pencil or pen. The verb is at tegne (to draw).

sentence.da: Man laver en **tegning** med en blyant.
sentence.en: You make a drawing with a pencil.

en tekande.explanation: "En tekande" means "a teapot", the pot you make and pour tea from.

sentence.da: Jeg brygger te i en **tekande**.
sentence.en: I brew tea in a teapot.

en teknologi.explanation: "En teknologi" means "a technology", a tool or method built with science: Teknologien udvikler sig hurtigt (The technology is developing fast). Without en, teknologi means technology in general: ny teknologi (new technology).

sentence.da: Ny **teknologi** gør livet nemmere for mange.
sentence.en: New technology makes life easier for many.

en tekst.explanation: "En tekst" means "a text", any piece of written words. It also means the words of a song (lyrics) and the words under a film: undertekster (subtitles).

sentence.da: En **tekst** kan være en artikel eller en besked.
sentence.en: A text can be an article or a message.

en tekstforfatter.explanation: "En tekstforfatter" means "a lyricist" or "a copywriter", so it covers two jobs: someone who writes the words for songs, and someone who writes texts for ads and companies. Context shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Hun er **tekstforfatter** og skriver ord til andres melodier.
sentence.en: She is a lyricist and writes words for other people's melodies.

en telefon.explanation: "En telefon" means "a phone". A mobile phone is en mobiltelefon or, more often, just en mobil. To call someone, say at ringe til: Jeg ringer til dig (I will call you).

sentence.da: Med en **telefon** kan jeg ringe hjem.
sentence.en: With a phone I can call home.

en temperatur.explanation: "En temperatur" means "a temperature", how hot or cold something is. For a high body temperature when you are ill, say at have feber (to have a fever).

sentence.da: Tyve grader er en god **temperatur**.
sentence.en: Twenty degrees is a good temperature.

en tendens.explanation: "En tendens" means "a trend" or "a tendency", the way something is slowly heading. It is often followed by til: en tendens til stress (a tendency toward stress).

sentence.da: Der er en **tendens** til, at priserne stiger hvert år.
sentence.en: There is a tendency for prices to rise every year.

en teori.explanation: "En teori" means "a theory", an idea that tries to explain something. It is also the opposite of practice: teori og praksis (theory and practice).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **teori**, men jeg kan ikke bevise den.
sentence.en: I have a theory, but I can't prove it.

en tepose.explanation: "En tepose" means "a tea bag", built from te (tea) and pose (bag). Pose is the usual word for a bag, as in en indkøbspose (a shopping bag).

sentence.da: Jeg putter en **tepose** i det varme vand.
sentence.en: I put a tea bag in the hot water.

en terapeut.explanation: "En terapeut" means "a therapist", a trained person who helps people with emotional problems by talking, or with physical problems by treatment, for example en fysioterapeut (a physical therapist).

sentence.da: Min **terapeut** hjælper mig med at tale om mine bekymringer.
sentence.en: My therapist helps me talk about my worries.

en termin.explanation: "En termin" means "a due date", especially for a baby: Barnets termin er i maj (The baby's due date is in May). It also means a fixed date for paying a part of a debt, such as a loan.

sentence.da: Næste **termin** på lånet skal betales den første i måneden.
sentence.en: The next installment on the loan must be paid on the first of the month.

en termokande.explanation: "En termokande" means "a thermos", an insulated jug that keeps drinks hot. It is built from termo (heat) and kande (jug).

sentence.da: Vi har kaffe i en **termokande** på turen.
sentence.en: We have coffee in a thermos on the trip.

en termokop.explanation: "En termokop" means "a travel mug", an insulated cup with a lid that you carry a hot drink in, for example on the way to work.

sentence.da: Min **termokop** holder kaffen varm i flere timer.
sentence.en: My travel mug keeps the coffee warm for several hours.

en terning.explanation: "En terning" means "a die" in games, and also "a cube". In cooking it means a small cube: en bouillonterning (a bouillon cube).

sentence.da: Du skal slå med en **terning**, og så flytter du brikken.
sentence.en: You roll a die, and then you move the piece.

en terrasse.explanation: "En terrasse" means "a terrace", a paved area next to a house where you sit outside. A cafe can have one too, for outdoor seating.

sentence.da: Huset har en **terrasse** med havemøbler.
sentence.en: The house has a terrace with garden furniture.

en terrorist.explanation: "En terrorist" means "a terrorist", a person who plans violent attacks for a political cause. The act is terrorisme (terrorism).

sentence.da: En **terrorist** bruger vold og gør folk bange.
sentence.en: A terrorist uses violence and scares people.

en teske.explanation: "En teske" means "a teaspoon", both the small spoon and the amount in recipes. It is built from te (tea) and ske (spoon).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **teske** sukker i min kaffe.
sentence.en: I take a teaspoon of sugar in my coffee.

en tid.explanation: "En tid" means "a time" or "time" in general. Danish splits what English calls time: en gang (one occasion, as in once or twice) and en time (an hour) are other words. To ask the clock time, say Hvad er klokken? (What time is it?).

sentence.da: Det tager lang **tid** at lære dansk.
sentence.en: It takes a long time to learn Danish.

en tid hos lægen.explanation: "En tid hos lægen" means "a doctor's appointment", literally a time at the doctor. En tid alone works for any booked time, such as one at the dentist or hairdresser.

forms.da: Jeg har en tid hos lægen.
Jeg skal have en tid hos lægen.
forms.en: I need to get a doctor's appointment.

sentence.da: Jeg har en **tid hos lægen** i dag.
sentence.en: I have a doctor's appointment today.

en tidsel.explanation: "En tidsel" means "a thistle", a wild plant that grows in fields and along roads. It is often seen as a weed because it spreads easily among crops.

sentence.da: En **tidsel** har skarpe pigge og en lilla blomst.
sentence.en: A thistle has sharp spikes and a purple flower.

en tidsfrist.explanation: "En tidsfrist" means "a time limit", the last moment by which something must be done or handed in. You keep it with at overholde tidsfristen (to meet the time limit) and break it with at overskride tidsfristen (to go past the time limit).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder hurtigt, fordi vi har en **tidsfrist** på fredag.
sentence.en: We work fast because we have a deadline on Friday.

en tidsplan.explanation: "En tidsplan" means "a schedule", a plan for when things happen. It is built from tid (time) and plan (plan).

sentence.da: Vi har en stram **tidsplan** i denne uge.
sentence.en: We have a tight schedule this week.

en tidszone.explanation: "En tidszone" means "a time zone", an area of the world that uses the same clock time. When you fly far east or west, the time changes.

sentence.da: Sverige er i samme **tidszone** som Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is in the same time zone as Denmark.

en tiger.explanation: "En tiger" means "a tiger", a big wild cat with orange fur and black stripes. The g is silent, so it sounds roughly like TEE-uh.

sentence.da: En **tiger** er en stor kat med striber.
sentence.en: A tiger is a big cat with stripes.

en tigger.explanation: "En tigger" means "a beggar", a person who asks strangers for money or food, usually on the street. The matching verb is at tigge (to beg): at tigge penge (to beg for money).

sentence.da: En **tigger** sidder på gaden med en kop til mønter.
sentence.en: A beggar sits on the street with a cup for coins.

en tilbagebetaling.explanation: "En tilbagebetaling" means "a refund" or "a repayment", money that is paid back to the person who gave it. A shop does it when you return something, and a person does it when paying back borrowed money.

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **tilbagebetaling** for den ødelagte vare.
sentence.en: I got a refund for the broken item.

en tilbagegang.explanation: "En tilbagegang" means "a decline", a drop in something over time, such as sales, health or numbers. Its opposite is fremgang (progress).

sentence.da: Butikken har haft en **tilbagegang** i salget i flere måneder.
sentence.en: The shop has had a decline in sales for several months.

en tilbagemelding.explanation: "En tilbagemelding" means "feedback", a response that tells someone how their work or idea was received. It can also be a simple answer, as in Jeg giver dig en tilbagemelding i morgen (I will get back to you tomorrow).

sentence.da: Chefen gav mig en **tilbagemelding** på rapporten, og den var positiv.
sentence.en: The boss gave me feedback on the report, and it was positive.

en tilbagevenden.explanation: "En tilbagevenden" means "a return", the act of coming back to a place, a situation or an earlier state. It is a formal, written word, often used with til: tilbagevenden til hjemlandet (the return to the home country). In everyday speech, Danes say at komme tilbage (to come back).

sentence.da: Folk ventede spændt på musikerens **tilbagevenden** efter ti år.
sentence.en: People waited excitedly for the musician's return after ten years.

en tilbudsavis.explanation: "En tilbudsavis" means "a flyer with offers". It is built from tilbud (offer) and avis (newspaper). Stores send it to your mailbox, and it is usually free.

sentence.da: En **tilbudsavis** viser ugens billige varer.
sentence.en: A flyer with offers shows the week's cheap goods.

en tilføjelse.explanation: "En tilføjelse" means "an addition", something extra put onto what already exists, like a note, a rule or a new part of a text. It belongs to at tilføje (to add).

sentence.da: Den nye **tilføjelse** til huset er et lyst køkken.
sentence.en: The new addition to the house is a bright kitchen.

en tilgang.explanation: "En tilgang" means "an approach", the way you handle a problem or a subject. It is often followed by til: en tilgang til undervisning (an approach to teaching).

sentence.da: Min **tilgang** til problemet er at tage ét skridt ad gangen.
sentence.en: My approach to the problem is to take one step at a time.

en tilhænger.explanation: "En tilhænger" means "a supporter", someone who believes in an idea, a person or a political party. For a sports team, Danes usually say en fan (a fan) instead.

sentence.da: Hun er en stor **tilhænger** af den nye lov.
sentence.en: She is a big supporter of the new law.

en tilhører.explanation: "En tilhører" means "a listener", a person who listens to someone talking, for example at a lecture or on the radio. Do not mix it up with tilhører as a form of at tilhøre (to belong to): Bogen tilhører mig (The book belongs to me).

sentence.da: En **tilhører** sidder stille og lytter til foredraget.
sentence.en: A listener sits quietly and listens to the talk.

en tilkørsel.explanation: "En tilkørsel" means "an on-ramp", the short road that leads you onto a big, fast road. It is built from til (to) and kørsel (driving). It can also mean any access road that leads up to a place, such as the road to a factory.

sentence.da: En **tilkørsel** fører dig op på motorvejen.
sentence.en: An on-ramp leads you up onto the highway.

en tilladelse.explanation: "En tilladelse" means "a permission", and also "a permit", an OK to do something. Said in general, it comes without en: Du skal have tilladelse (You need permission). With en it is often a written permit: en tilladelse til at fiske (a permit to fish).

sentence.da: Du må ikke bygge uden **tilladelse** fra kommunen.
sentence.en: You may not build without permission from the municipality.

en tilmelding.explanation: "En tilmelding" means "a registration / sign-up", when you put your name down for a course or an event. The matching verb is at tilmelde sig (to sign up).

sentence.da: **Tilmelding** er åben indtil fredag.
sentence.en: Sign-up is open until Friday.

en tilpasning.explanation: "En tilpasning" means "an adaptation", the process of altering something, or yourself, to fit a new situation. It is often used without en for the general idea.

sentence.da: Det kræver **tilpasning** at flytte til et nyt land.
sentence.en: It takes adaptation to move to a new country.

en tilskuer.explanation: "En tilskuer" means "a spectator", a person who watches an event, such as a match or a show.

sentence.da: En **tilskuer** ser kampen, men spiller ikke selv.
sentence.en: A spectator watches the match but does not play.

en tilstand.explanation: "En tilstand" means "a condition" or "a state", how a person or thing is at a given moment: Patientens tilstand er stabil (The patient's condition is stable). It is not used for a country as a government, which is en stat.

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men den er i god **tilstand**.
sentence.en: The car is old, but it is in good condition.

en tilståelse.explanation: "En tilståelse" means "a confession", a statement in which someone owns up to having done something wrong, especially to the police or in court. The verb is at tilstå: Han tilstod (He confessed).

sentence.da: Politiet fik en **tilståelse** efter flere timers afhøring.
sentence.en: The police got a confession after several hours of questioning.

en tiltalt.explanation: "En tiltalt" means "a defendant", a person who is on trial for a crime. The same word is used for being charged: Han er tiltalt for tyveri (He is charged with theft).

sentence.da: I retten sidder en **tiltalt** ved siden af sin forsvarer.
sentence.en: In the courtroom, a defendant sits next to his defense attorney.

en tiltrækning.explanation: "En tiltrækning" means "an attraction", a pull toward something or someone, like the pull between two people.

sentence.da: Der var en stærk **tiltrækning** mellem dem fra første møde.
sentence.en: There was a strong attraction between them from the first meeting.

en tilvænning.explanation: "En tilvænning" means "an adjustment", the time it takes to get used to something new, such as a new job or home. It belongs to at vænne sig til (to get used to).

sentence.da: Det kræver **tilvænning** at starte i en ny børnehave.
sentence.en: It takes some adjustment to start in a new kindergarten.

en time.explanation: "En time" means "an hour". It also means a lesson or class, so en dansktime is a Danish lesson. Om en time means "in an hour". For time in general, say tid (time).

sentence.da: Der er tres minutter i en **time**.
sentence.en: There are sixty minutes in an hour.

en ting.explanation: "En ting" means "a thing". Hvad er det for en ting? (What is that thing?) is a common way to ask about something you do not recognize.

sentence.da: Jeg har mange **ting** i min taske.
sentence.en: I have many things in my bag.

en titel.explanation: "En titel" means "a title", the name of a book, film or song. It is also a rank or job name: Hun har titlen professor (She has the title of professor).

sentence.da: Du kan læse bogens **titel** på forsiden.
sentence.en: You can read the book's title on the cover.

en titelsang.explanation: "En titelsang" means "a theme song", the song that plays at the start of a movie or a show. It is built from en titel (a title) and en sang (a song).

sentence.da: Serien starter med en **titelsang**, og jeg synger med.
sentence.en: The series starts with a theme song, and I sing along.

en tjener.explanation: "En tjener" means "a waiter", for men and women alike. It can also mean "a servant".

sentence.da: En **tjener** bringer maden til bordet.
sentence.en: A waiter brings the food to the table.

en tjeneste.explanation: "En tjeneste" means "a favor" and also "a service": Jeg skylder dig en tjeneste (I owe you a favor). Banken tilbyder en ny tjeneste (The bank offers a new service).

sentence.da: Kan du gøre mig en **tjeneste**?
sentence.en: Can you do me a favor?

en toast.explanation: "En toast" means "a toasted sandwich", a sandwich that is pressed and heated, usually with cheese inside. Plain toasted bread is ristet brød (toasted bread).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **toast** med skinke og ost.
sentence.en: I would like a toasted sandwich with ham and cheese.

en togbillet.explanation: "En togbillet" means "a train ticket", built from tog (train) and billet (ticket). Other tickets work the same way: en busbillet (a bus ticket).

sentence.da: Med en **togbillet** kan du køre med toget.
sentence.en: With a train ticket you can ride the train.

en togfører.explanation: "En togfører" means "a train conductor", the person in charge of a train and its passengers. The conductor is not the one driving, who is called en lokomotivfører (a train driver).

sentence.da: Vores **togfører** siger, at toget er forsinket.
sentence.en: Our conductor says that the train is delayed.

en togrejse.explanation: "En togrejse" means "a train journey". It is built from tog (train) and rejse (journey). Rejse is also a verb, at rejse (to travel): Jeg rejser med tog (I travel by train).

sentence.da: Vi ser landet fra vinduet på en **togrejse**.
sentence.en: We see the country from the window on a train journey.

en togstation.explanation: "En togstation" means "a train station", built from tog (train) and station (station). You say på togstationen (at the train station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget ved en **togstation**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a train station.

en toiletbørste.explanation: "En toiletbørste" means "a toilet brush", used to clean inside the toilet. It is built from toilet (toilet) and børste (brush).

sentence.da: Jeg gør toilettet rent med en **toiletbørste**.
sentence.en: I clean the toilet with a toilet brush.

en toldkontrol.explanation: "En toldkontrol" means "a customs check", where officers look at what you bring into a country. It is built from told (customs) and kontrol (check).

sentence.da: Vi skal igennem en **toldkontrol** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We have to go through a customs check at the airport.

en tolk.explanation: "En tolk" means "an interpreter", a person who translates speech out loud, on the spot, so that two people who do not understand each other can talk. Written texts are handled by en oversætter (a translator).

sentence.da: Vi bad en **tolk** om at oversætte, fordi vi ikke talte dansk.
sentence.en: We asked an interpreter to translate because we did not speak Danish.

en tolkning.explanation: "En tolkning" means "an interpretation", a personal reading of something unclear, such as a text, a law or a dream. It is also a performance of a piece of music or a role: skuespillerens tolkning af Hamlet (the actor's take on Hamlet).

sentence.da: Hver læser har sin egen **tolkning** af digtet.
sentence.en: Every reader has their own interpretation of the poem.

en tomat.explanation: "En tomat" means "a tomato". It joins with other words: tomatsuppe (tomato soup) and tomatsovs (tomato sauce).

sentence.da: En **tomat** er rød og rund.
sentence.en: A tomato is red and round.

en tombola.explanation: "En tombola" means "a raffle", a game where you buy a numbered ticket and win a gift if your number is drawn. It is common at school fairs and club events.

sentence.da: Der er **tombola** til festen, og alle kan vinde noget.
sentence.en: There is a raffle at the party, and everyone can win something.

en tommelfinger.explanation: "En tommelfinger" means "a thumb". Tommelfinger op means "thumbs up". Danish says the thumb instead of my thumb: Jeg har ondt i tommelfingeren (My thumb hurts, literally I have pain in the thumb).

sentence.da: Din **tommelfinger** er den korteste og tykkeste finger.
sentence.en: Your thumb is the shortest and thickest finger.

en top.explanation: "En top" means "a top", a light piece of clothing with thin straps or no sleeves. The same word also means the top of something: toppen af bjerget (the top of the mountain).

sentence.da: Det er varmt, og hun tager en **top** på.
sentence.en: It is warm, and she puts on a top.

en torn.explanation: "En torn" means "a thorn", a sharp point that grows on a plant. It also appears in en torn i øjet (a thorn in the eye), about something that keeps annoying you.

sentence.da: Rosen har en skarp **torn** på stilken, og den kan stikke.
sentence.en: The rose has a sharp thorn on the stem, and it can prick.

en tornado.explanation: "En tornado" means "a tornado", a narrow, spinning column of wind that reaches from a thundercloud down to the ground. It is much smaller and shorter than en orkan (a hurricane), which is a huge system of wind and rain.

sentence.da: En **tornado** kan rive huse op og kaste biler gennem luften.
sentence.en: A tornado can tear houses up and throw cars through the air.

en tortilla.explanation: "En tortilla" means "a tortilla", a thin round flatbread that is filled and rolled or folded.

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **tortilla** med bønner og ost.
sentence.en: I fill a tortilla with beans and cheese.

en torvehal.explanation: "En torvehal" means "a market hall", a covered building with many food stalls, like Torvehallerne in Copenhagen.

sentence.da: Vi spiser frokost i en **torvehal** i København.
sentence.en: We eat lunch in a market hall in Copenhagen.

en tradition.explanation: "En tradition" means "a tradition", something a family or country does year after year.

sentence.da: Det er en gammel **tradition** i vores familie.
sentence.en: It is an old tradition in our family.

en tragedie.explanation: "En tragedie" means "a tragedy", a terrible event with great loss. It is also a serious play with a sad ending, the opposite of en komedie (a comedy).

sentence.da: Branden i skolen var en **tragedie** for hele byen.
sentence.en: The fire at the school was a tragedy for the whole town.

en traktat.explanation: "En traktat" means "a treaty", a formal written deal between countries that they promise to follow. For a deal between people or companies, use en aftale (an agreement) instead.

sentence.da: Landene underskrev en **traktat** og lovede at holde freden.
sentence.en: The countries signed a treaty and promised to keep the peace.

en traktor.explanation: "En traktor" means "a tractor", the big farm vehicle with large rear wheels. It pulls heavy loads and tools across the fields.

sentence.da: Landmanden kører **traktor** hen over marken.
sentence.en: The farmer drives a tractor across the field.

en trang.explanation: "En trang" means "an urge", a strong wish from inside to do or have something, usually followed by til (to): en trang til sødt (a craving for sweets). As a describing word, trang means narrow: et trangt rum (a narrow room).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en pludselig **trang** til at synge.
sentence.en: I suddenly felt an urge to sing.

en transaktion.explanation: "En transaktion" means "a transaction", one single movement of money, such as a card purchase or a deposit. Each line in your online bank is one transaktion.

sentence.da: Banken har stoppet min **transaktion**, fordi kortet var spærret.
sentence.en: The bank stopped my transaction because the card was blocked.

en trappe.explanation: "En trappe" means "a staircase" or "stairs": Jeg går op ad trappen (I walk up the stairs). Down is ned ad trappen (down the stairs).

sentence.da: Der er en **trappe** ned til kælderen.
sentence.en: There is a staircase down to the basement.

en tredjedel.explanation: "En tredjedel" means "a third", one of three equal parts. It is built from tredje (third) and del (part).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst en **tredjedel** af bogen.
sentence.en: I have read a third of the book.

en trekant.explanation: "En trekant" means "a triangle", a shape with three straight sides. It is built from tre (three) and kant (edge).

sentence.da: Tegn en **trekant** med tre hjørner.
sentence.en: Draw a triangle with three corners.

en tremmeseng.explanation: "En tremmeseng" means "a crib", a baby bed with bars on the sides. It is built from tremmer (bars) and seng (bed).

sentence.da: Den lille sover i en **tremmeseng** ved siden af os.
sentence.en: The little one sleeps in a crib next to us.

en trillebør.explanation: "En trillebør" means "a wheelbarrow", a small cart with one wheel in front and two handles, used in the garden or on building sites to carry heavy loads. The first part comes from at trille (to roll).

sentence.da: Jeg flytter jorden i haven med en **trillebør**.
sentence.en: I move the soil in the garden with a wheelbarrow.

en troldmand.explanation: "En troldmand" means "a wizard", a man in stories who can do magic. It is built from trold (troll) and mand (man).

sentence.da: En **troldmand** kan trylle med en tryllestav.
sentence.en: A wizard can do magic with a magic wand.

en tromme.explanation: "En tromme" means "a drum", an instrument you hit to make a beat. A person who plays it is en trommeslager (a drummer).

sentence.da: Man slår på en **tromme** med to stave.
sentence.en: You hit a drum with two sticks.

en trompet.explanation: "En trompet" means "a trumpet". To say you play it, leave out en: Han spiller trompet (He plays the trumpet).

sentence.da: Min onkel spiller **trompet** i et orkester.
sentence.en: My uncle plays the trumpet in an orchestra.

en trone.explanation: "En trone" means "a throne", the grand chair of a king or queen. It also stands for royal power itself: at arve tronen (to inherit the throne).

sentence.da: Kongen sidder på sin **trone** i den store sal.
sentence.en: The king sits on his throne in the big hall.

en trop.explanation: "En trop" means "a troop", a group of fighters or scouts. Most often you see the plural tropper (troops), for example when a country sends soldiers abroad.

sentence.da: Hver **trop** af spejdere har sin egen leder.
sentence.en: Each troop of scouts has its own leader.

en trussel.explanation: "En trussel" means "a threat", something that might cause harm. It also works for something that puts nature or people at risk: en trussel mod miljøet (a threat to the environment).

sentence.da: Det er en **trussel**, når nogen vil gøre dig ondt.
sentence.en: It is a threat when someone wants to hurt you.

en trækfugl.explanation: "En trækfugl" means "a migratory bird", a bird that flies far away for the winter and comes back in spring. Here træk is the yearly journey, the same word as in at trække (to pull).

sentence.da: Svalen er en **trækfugl**, og den flyver til Afrika om vinteren.
sentence.en: The swallow is a migratory bird, and it flies to Africa in the winter.

en træner.explanation: "En træner" means "a coach", the person who leads a team or a workout. It comes from at træne (to train).

sentence.da: Vores **træner** er meget god til at forklare.
sentence.en: Our coach is very good at explaining.

en trøje.explanation: "En trøje" means "a sweater" or "a jumper". Danes also use it for other tops, such as en fodboldtrøje (a soccer shirt).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **trøje** på.
sentence.en: I am wearing a warm sweater.

en tudse.explanation: "En tudse" means "a toad". It looks like en frø (a frog) but spends more time on land.

sentence.da: En **tudse** har tør, knoldet hud og lever mest på land.
sentence.en: A toad has dry, bumpy skin and lives mostly on land.

en tulipan.explanation: "En tulipan" means "a tulip", a flower with a cup-shaped bloom in many colors.

sentence.da: En **tulipan** blomstrer om foråret og kommer fra et løg.
sentence.en: A tulip blooms in spring and grows from a bulb.

en tunge.explanation: "En tunge" means "a tongue", the one in your mouth. At række tunge means "to stick out your tongue".

sentence.da: Lægen sagde: Vis mig din **tunge**.
sentence.en: The doctor said: Show me your tongue.

en tunnel.explanation: "En tunnel" means "a tunnel", a road or train track that goes under the ground, a mountain or the water.

sentence.da: Toget kører gennem en lang **tunnel** under havet.
sentence.en: The train goes through a long tunnel under the sea.

en tur.explanation: "En tur" means "a trip" or "a turn". You say at gå en tur (to go for a walk), at tage på tur (to go on a trip) and Det er din tur (It is your turn). A longer, bigger journey is en rejse (a journey).
