sentence.da: Vi går en **tur** i parken.
sentence.en: We are going for a walk in the park.

en turist.explanation: "En turist" means "a tourist", someone who visits a place for fun. A person who lives there is en indbygger (a resident).

sentence.da: Som **turist** vil jeg se hele byen.
sentence.en: As a tourist, I want to see the whole city.

en turistattraktion.explanation: "En turistattraktion" means "a tourist attraction", a place many visitors come to see. A shorter word is en seværdighed (a sight).

sentence.da: Den gamle bro er en kendt **turistattraktion**.
sentence.en: The old bridge is a famous tourist attraction.

en turnering.explanation: "En turnering" means "a tournament", a competition in several rounds, in sports or in games such as chess, ending with a winner.

sentence.da: Vi skal spille tre kampe i en **turnering** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We will play three matches in a tournament this weekend.

en tusch.explanation: "En tusch" means "a marker", a pen with thick colored ink. A thin pen for writing is en kuglepen (a ballpoint pen).

sentence.da: Børnene tegner med en rød **tusch**.
sentence.en: The children draw with a red marker.

en tv-kanal.explanation: "En tv-kanal" means "a TV channel", a station that sends out programs. Danes often say just kanal (channel): Skift kanal (Change the channel).

sentence.da: På en **tv-kanal** kan du se programmer.
sentence.en: On a TV channel you can watch programs.

en tv-serie.explanation: "En tv-serie" means "a TV series", a show with many episodes. One episode is et afsnit: Vi ser to afsnit i weekenden (We watch two episodes on the weekend).

sentence.da: Jeg ser en ny **tv-serie** om en detektiv.
sentence.en: I am watching a new TV series about a detective.

en tvetydighed.explanation: "En tvetydighed" means "an ambiguity", something that can be understood in two ways. It is literally a two-meaning thing. Compare en uklarhed (a lack of clarity), where something is simply not settled.

sentence.da: Sætningen har en **tvetydighed**, fordi man kan læse den på to måder.
sentence.en: The sentence has an ambiguity because you can read it in two ways.

en tvilling.explanation: "En tvilling" means "a twin", one of two children born at the same time. The same word is used for boys and girls.

sentence.da: Hun er **tvilling**, og hendes søster ligner hende.
sentence.en: She is a twin, and her sister looks like her.

en tvivl.explanation: "En tvivl" means "a doubt". It is mostly used in set phrases: Der er ingen tvivl (There is no doubt) and Jeg har ingen tvivl (I have no doubt).

sentence.da: Jeg er i **tvivl** og kan ikke vælge.
sentence.en: I am in doubt and cannot choose.

en type.explanation: "En type" means "a type" or "a kind": Hvilken type bil har du? (What type of car do you have?) It is also informal for "a guy": en mærkelig type (a strange guy).

sentence.da: Han er en meget flink **type**.
sentence.en: He is a very nice guy.

en tyr.explanation: "En tyr" means "a bull", a full-grown male of cattle, kept for breeding. Tyren (the Bull) is also the star sign Taurus.

sentence.da: En **tyr** er hannen, og en ko er hunnen.
sentence.en: A bull is the male, and a cow is the female.

en tyrekalv.explanation: "En tyrekalv" means "a bull calf", a young male of cattle. The female version is en kvigekalv (a heifer calf).

sentence.da: Landmanden har en ko og en **tyrekalv** i stalden.
sentence.en: The farmer has a cow and a bull calf in the barn.

en tyrker.explanation: "En tyrker" means "a Turk", a person from Turkey. The country is Tyrkiet, and the Danish word for Turkish is tyrkisk. Danish writes nationalities with a small letter: en tyrker.

sentence.da: Min nabo er **tyrker**, og han kommer fra Istanbul.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a Turk, and he comes from Istanbul.

en tysker.explanation: "En tysker" means "a German", a person from Germany. The word is used for both men and women. You can say either Jeg er tysker or Jeg er tysk (I am German).

sentence.da: Hun er **tysker** og bor i Tyskland.
sentence.en: She is German and lives in Germany.

en tyv.explanation: "En tyv" means "a thief", someone who steals. The action is at stjæle (to steal).

sentence.da: En **tyv** har taget min cykel fra gården.
sentence.en: A thief has taken my bike from the yard.

en tå.explanation: "En tå" means "a toe", one of the five at the end of each foot. To walk on tiptoe, say at gå på tæer (to walk on toes).

sentence.da: Din **tå** sidder for enden af din fod.
sentence.en: Your toe sits at the end of your foot.

en tåbe.explanation: "En tåbe" means "a fool", someone who acts without thinking. The matching describing word is tåbelig: Det var tåbeligt (That was foolish).

sentence.da: Kun en **tåbe** går ud på den tynde is.
sentence.en: Only a fool walks out on the thin ice.

en tåre.explanation: "En tåre" means "a tear", a drop of water that runs down your cheek when you are very sad, happy or moved.

sentence.da: Hun græd, og der løb en **tåre** ned ad kinden.
sentence.en: She cried and a tear ran down her cheek.

en tændstik.explanation: "En tændstik" means "a match" for lighting a fire. A match in sports is en kamp (a game), so the two are not the same word.

sentence.da: Jeg tænder bålet med en **tændstik**.
sentence.en: I light the fire with a match.

en tærskel.explanation: "En tærskel" means "a threshold". Besides the doorway, it is used for a limit that you cross: en smertetærskel (a pain threshold).

sentence.da: Det lave stykke i gulvet under en døråbning er en **tærskel**.
sentence.en: The low piece in the floor under a doorway is a threshold.

en tøjbutik.explanation: "En tøjbutik" means "a clothing store". It is made from tøj (clothes) and butik (shop), and Danish often joins words like this: en skobutik (a shoe store).

sentence.da: Jeg køber bukser i en **tøjbutik**.
sentence.en: I buy trousers in a clothing store.

en tøjbøjle.explanation: "En tøjbøjle" means "a clothes hanger", the frame you hang a shirt, jacket or dress on. It is often shortened to en bøjle.

sentence.da: Skjorten hænger på en **tøjbøjle** i skabet.
sentence.en: The shirt hangs on a clothes hanger in the closet.

en tøjkurv.explanation: "En tøjkurv" means "a laundry basket", the basket where dirty clothes wait until you wash them. It is tøj (clothes) plus kurv (basket).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger de beskidte sokker i min **tøjkurv**.
sentence.en: I put the dirty socks in my laundry basket.

en tøjstørrelse.explanation: "En tøjstørrelse" means "a clothing size", for example S, M or L. It is built from tøj (clothes) and størrelse (size).

sentence.da: Min **tøjstørrelse** er M, men jeg vil gerne prøve L.
sentence.en: My clothing size is M, but I would like to try L.

en tøjvask.explanation: "En tøjvask" means "a laundry", one load of dirty clothes. It is the job itself, not the place, which is et vaskeri (a laundry business).

sentence.da: Jeg skal lave en **tøjvask**, fordi kurven er fuld.
sentence.en: I need to do a load of laundry because the basket is full.

en tømrer.explanation: "En tømrer" means "a carpenter", someone who builds with wood, like roofs and house frames. For furniture, Danes say en snedker (a cabinetmaker).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **tømrer** og arbejder med træ.
sentence.en: My uncle is a carpenter and works with wood.

en tønde.explanation: "En tønde" means "a barrel", a large round container made of wooden boards, used for beer or oil. At the Danish carnival Fastelavn, children slå katten af tønden (knock the cat out of the barrel), which means hitting a barrel full of sweets until it breaks open.

sentence.da: Vinen ligger i en **tønde** af egetræ i kælderen.
sentence.en: The wine lies in an oak barrel in the cellar.

en tørke.explanation: "En tørke" means "a drought", a long period with little or no rain, which is hard on farmers.

sentence.da: Landmændene mister afgrøder, når en **tørke** varer i flere måneder.
sentence.en: Farmers lose crops when a drought lasts for several months.

en tørresnor.explanation: "En tørresnor" means "a clothesline", a cord you hang wet clothes on to dry, usually outside in a garden or on a balcony. The clothes are held in place with clothespins.

sentence.da: Jeg hænger vasketøjet op på en **tørresnor**.
sentence.en: I hang the laundry up on a clothesline.

en tørretumbler.explanation: "En tørretumbler" means "a dryer", a machine that dries clothes with warm air. A tørresnor (clothesline) does the same job outside, without a machine.

sentence.da: Vi har ikke en **tørretumbler**, så tøjet hænger ude.
sentence.en: We do not have a dryer, so the clothes hang outside.

en tøven.explanation: "En tøven" means "a hesitation", a short wait before you act because you are unsure. It comes from at tøve (to hesitate), and it is mostly used without en, after a word like med (with) or uden (without).

sentence.da: Hun sagde ja uden **tøven**, fordi hun var helt sikker.
sentence.en: She said yes without hesitation because she was completely sure.

et tag.explanation: "Et tag" means "a roof". The same word is also the order Tag! (Take!): Tag en kage! (Take a cake!)

sentence.da: Huset har et rødt **tag**.
sentence.en: The house has a red roof.

et takeaway.explanation: "Et takeaway" means "a takeout meal", food you buy ready-made and eat at home. Many places also deliver: De leverer takeaway (They deliver takeout).

sentence.da: Vi bestiller **takeaway** i aften, fordi vi er trætte.
sentence.en: We are ordering takeout tonight because we are tired.

et takkekort.explanation: "Et takkekort" means "a thank-you card", a card you send or give to thank someone, for example after a gift, a party or a wedding.

sentence.da: Hun skrev et **takkekort** til sin lærer, fordi han hjalp hende.
sentence.en: She wrote a thank-you card to her teacher because he helped her.

et tal.explanation: "Et tal" means "a number", like 5 or 12, that you count or calculate with. For a phone number or house number, Danes use et nummer instead.

sentence.da: Fem er et lille **tal**.
sentence.en: Five is a small number.

et talent.explanation: "Et talent" means "a talent", something you are naturally good at without much effort. A person with talent is talentfuld (talented).

sentence.da: Hun har et stort **talent** for musik.
sentence.en: She has a great talent for music.

et talkshow.explanation: "Et talkshow" means "a talk show", a TV or radio show where the person leading it talks with guests about news, culture or their lives.

sentence.da: Skuespilleren var gæst i et **talkshow** i går aftes.
sentence.en: The actor was a guest on a talk show last night.

et tandkrus.explanation: "Et tandkrus" means "a toothbrush cup", the small cup by the bathroom sink where you keep your brush.

sentence.da: Jeg putter tandbørsten i et blåt **tandkrus**.
sentence.en: I put the toothbrush in a blue toothbrush cup.

et tastatur.explanation: "Et tastatur" means "a keyboard", the keys you type on. A key you press is en tast, while a key for a lock is en nøgle (a key).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver hurtigt på mit nye **tastatur**.
sentence.en: I type fast on my new keyboard.

et team.explanation: "Et team" means "a team" at work or on a project. For a sports team, et hold (a team) is more common.

sentence.da: Mit **team** arbejder sammen om et nyt projekt.
sentence.en: My team is working together on a new project.

et teater.explanation: "Et teater" means "a theater", both the building and the art form. A film is shown in a movie theater (en biograf), not et teater.

sentence.da: Vi ser et skuespil i et stort **teater** i aften.
sentence.en: We are watching a play in a big theater tonight.

et teaterstykke.explanation: "Et teaterstykke" means "a stage play", a story written to be performed by actors in front of an audience. A film is not a teaterstykke, because it is recorded and not played live.

sentence.da: Et **teaterstykke** bliver spillet live foran et publikum.
sentence.en: A stage play is performed live in front of an audience.

et tegn.explanation: "Et tegn" means "a sign", something that shows what is happening or what will happen: Det er et godt tegn (That is a good sign). Der er tegn på regn (There are signs of rain).

sentence.da: Hendes smil er et godt **tegn**.
sentence.en: Her smile is a good sign.

et telefonnummer.explanation: "Et telefonnummer" means "a phone number", the number you call to reach someone. It is built from telefon (phone) and nummer (number), the same nummer as in et husnummer (a house number).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til ham på hans **telefonnummer**.
sentence.en: I call him on his phone number.

et telt.explanation: "Et telt" means "a tent". To put it up, say at slå et telt op (to pitch a tent). Op adds the idea of up, as in at skrive op (to write down) and at ringe op (to call up).

sentence.da: Vi sover i et **telt** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are sleeping in a tent this weekend.

et tema.explanation: "Et tema" means "a theme", the main subject or idea of a text, a film, a class or an event: Temaet for festen er 80'erne (The theme of the party is the 80s).

sentence.da: Bogens **tema** er venskab og tab.
sentence.en: The theme of the book is friendship and loss.

et tempel.explanation: "Et tempel" means "a temple", a building for worship, especially in religions such as Buddhism and Hinduism. A Christian church is en kirke, not et tempel.

sentence.da: Munkene beder i et **tempel** hver morgen.
sentence.en: The monks pray in a temple every morning.

et temperament.explanation: "Et temperament" means "a temper" and "a temperament", a person's natural way of reacting, for example calm, lively or quick to get angry. A word for the feeling goes before it: et hidsigt temperament (a fiery temperament).

sentence.da: Hans **temperament** er så livligt, at han aldrig sidder stille.
sentence.en: His temperament is so lively that he never sits still.

et termometer.explanation: "Et termometer" means "a thermometer", something that shows how warm or cold it is, in the air or in your body.

sentence.da: Jeg henter et **termometer**, fordi jeg har feber.
sentence.en: I get a thermometer because I have a fever.

et territorium.explanation: "Et territorium" means "a territory", a piece of land that belongs to a state, a ruler or an animal. A territory can also be land that a state controls but that is not a full country.

sentence.da: Dyret forsvarer sit **territorium** mod andre dyr.
sentence.en: The animal defends its territory against other animals.

et testamente.explanation: "Et testamente" means "a will" and "a testament": a written document that says who will get your money and belongings after your death. Det Nye Testamente (the New Testament) is the second part of the Bible.

sentence.da: Hun skrev i sit **testamente**, at børnene skal arve huset.
sentence.en: She wrote in her will that the children shall inherit the house.

et tidsfordriv.explanation: "Et tidsfordriv" means "a pastime", something you do to fill free time, for fun or because you are waiting. It comes from at fordrive tiden (to pass the time).

sentence.da: Et krydsord er et godt **tidsfordriv** på en lang togtur.
sentence.en: A crossword is a good pastime on a long train ride.

et tidspunkt.explanation: "Et tidspunkt" means "a point in time", one exact moment, not a long period: På det tidspunkt var jeg hjemme (At that time I was at home).

sentence.da: Hvilket **tidspunkt** passer dig bedst?
sentence.en: Which time suits you best?

et tidsrum.explanation: "Et tidsrum" means "a period of time", a stretch with a clear start and end. Use it when you think of the whole stretch with two limits, not one point in time.

sentence.da: Butikken er lukket i et **tidsrum** mellem klokken tolv og et.
sentence.en: The shop is closed for a period between twelve and one o'clock.

et tilbageslag.explanation: "Et tilbageslag" means "a setback", something that pushes you back when things were going well, such as getting worse again after you had started to recover.

sentence.da: Fabrikkens lukning var et stort **tilbageslag** for hele byen.
sentence.en: The closing of the factory was a big setback for the whole town.

et tilbud.explanation: "Et tilbud" means "an offer" or "a deal". In a shop, på tilbud means "on sale", at a lower price for a short time.

sentence.da: Kaffe til 20 kroner er et godt **tilbud**.
sentence.en: Coffee for 20 kroner is a good deal.

et tilbudskatalog.explanation: "Et tilbudskatalog" means "a sale catalog", a booklet or web page that shows the shop's special prices.

sentence.da: Jeg kigger i et **tilbudskatalog** og finder billig mad.
sentence.en: I look in a sale catalog and find cheap food.

et tilfælde.explanation: "Et tilfælde" means "a case" or "a coincidence". Ved et tilfælde (By chance) means nobody planned it. For a case in court, use en sag (a case).

sentence.da: I dette **tilfælde** må vi vente.
sentence.en: In this case we have to wait.

et tilholdssted.explanation: "Et tilholdssted" means "a hangout" and "a haunt", a place where a person or a group often stays. It is built from at holde til (to stay somewhere), so it is the place where someone usually stays, and it can be used for people and animals.

sentence.da: Biblioteket er de unges faste **tilholdssted** efter skole.
sentence.en: The library is the young people's regular hangout after school.

et tillægsord.explanation: "Et tillægsord" means "an adjective", a word that describes a thing or a person, like stor (big) or glad (happy). The Danish name means roughly "addition word", because the word adds to the name of a thing.

sentence.da: Ordet stor er et **tillægsord**, fordi det beskriver en ting.
sentence.en: The word stor is an adjective because it describes a thing.

et tiltag.explanation: "Et tiltag" means "an initiative" and "a measure", a specific step that someone decides on to solve a problem or reach a goal. It is common in news and politics: nye tiltag mod trafikstøj (new measures against traffic noise).

sentence.da: Byen indfører et nyt **tiltag**: gratis bus for børn.
sentence.en: The city is introducing a new initiative: free buses for children.

et tip.explanation: "Et tip" means "a tip", a short, helpful suggestion. For money you leave for service, Danes say drikkepenge (tip money).

sentence.da: Min lærer gav mig et godt **tip** til eksamen.
sentence.en: My teacher gave me a good tip for the exam.

et tog.explanation: "Et tog" means "a train". To say you go by train, Danes say at tage toget (literally to take the train).

sentence.da: Vi tager et **tog** til København.
sentence.en: We take a train to Copenhagen.

et toilet.explanation: "Et toilet" means "a toilet", and also the room that has one. Hvor er toilettet? (Where is the toilet?) is how you ask for the restroom. On the doors, you see Herrer (men) and Damer (women).

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **toilet** og vaske hænder.
sentence.en: I am going to the restroom to wash my hands.

et topmøde.explanation: "Et topmøde" means "a summit", a meeting between the top leaders of countries or organizations, for example to discuss war, climate or trade.

sentence.da: Lederne mødes til et **topmøde** om klimaet i næste uge.
sentence.en: The leaders meet at a summit about the climate next week.

et tordenvejr.explanation: "Et tordenvejr" means "a thunderstorm", weather with thunder and heavy rain. It is built from torden (thunder) and vejr (weather), the same vejr as in regnvejr (rainy weather) and solskinsvejr (sunny weather).

sentence.da: Vi bliver inde, fordi der er **tordenvejr**.
sentence.en: We are staying inside because there is a thunderstorm.

et torv.explanation: "Et torv" means "a (market) square", an open space in a town where people meet and sell things.

sentence.da: Man køber frugt og grønt på et **torv**.
sentence.en: You buy fruit and vegetables at a square.

et trafiklys.explanation: "Et trafiklys" means "a traffic light". It is built from trafik (traffic) and lys (light). Lys also means a candle: et lys på bordet (a candle on the table).

sentence.da: Bilerne holder stille, når et **trafiklys** er rødt.
sentence.en: The cars stop when a traffic light is red.

et trick.explanation: "Et trick" means "a trick", a clever move that surprises people, like a card trick. To fool someone, use at narre (to fool).

sentence.da: Hunden lærer et nyt **trick**, og børnene klapper.
sentence.en: The dog learns a new trick, and the kids clap.

et trin.explanation: "Et trin" means "a step" on a stairway or a stage in a process: Der er fem trin op til døren (There are five steps up to the door). For a footstep, use et skridt (a step).

sentence.da: Vi tager det næste **trin** i planen.
sentence.en: We take the next step in the plan.

et tryk.explanation: "Et tryk" means "a pressure" or "a stress". It can be a push on something, as in et tryk på knappen (a press on the button) or blodtryk (blood pressure), and it is also the extra force on one part of a word when you speak.

sentence.da: Man lægger **tryk** på første del af ordet.
sentence.en: You put stress on the first part of the word.

et træ.explanation: "Et træ" means "a tree", and also "wood" as a material: et bord af træ (a table made of wood). For a large group of trees, Danes say en skov (a forest).

sentence.da: Æbler vokser på et **træ**.
sentence.en: Apples grow on a tree.

et træk.explanation: "Et træk" means "a move", one action in a game such as chess: Det var et smart træk (That was a smart move). It also means "a draft" of cold air, and "a pull" on a cigarette or a rope.

sentence.da: Det næste **træk** i skak kan afgøre hele spillet.
sentence.en: The next move in chess can decide the whole game.

et træningspas.explanation: "Et træningspas" means "a training session", one workout or practice, for example at a sports club. Træning (training) alone means exercising in general, while a træningspas is one single occasion.

sentence.da: Jeg har et **træningspas** hver tirsdag og torsdag.
sentence.en: I have a training session every Tuesday and Thursday.

et tv.explanation: "Et tv" means "a TV" and is said te-ve. Watching TV is at se tv (literally to see TV).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sofaen og ser **tv**.
sentence.en: I sit on the sofa and watch TV.

et tv-program.explanation: "Et tv-program" means "a TV program", one show on TV, for example about nature or food. A show with many episodes is en tv-serie (a TV series).

sentence.da: Der kommer et godt **tv-program** i aften.
sentence.en: A good TV program is coming on tonight.

et tyveri.explanation: "Et tyveri" means "a theft", when someone takes what is not theirs. The person who does it is en tyv (a thief).

sentence.da: Politiet kommer, fordi der er sket et **tyveri**.
sentence.en: The police are coming because a theft has happened.

et tårn.explanation: "Et tårn" means "a tower", a tall, narrow building or part of a building.

sentence.da: Der er en flot udsigt fra det høje **tårn**.
sentence.en: There is a nice view from the tall tower.

et tæppe.explanation: "Et tæppe" means both "a rug" and "a blanket": Der ligger et tæppe på gulvet (There is a rug on the floor). Jeg sidder i sofaen med et tæppe (I sit on the sofa with a blanket).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger et **tæppe** over benene.
sentence.en: I put a blanket over my legs.

et tørklæde.explanation: "Et tørklæde" means "a scarf". The second half is klæde (a cloth), which you also see in et håndklæde (a towel).

sentence.da: Jeg har et **tørklæde** om halsen.
sentence.en: I have a scarf around my neck.

et tørrestativ.explanation: "Et tørrestativ" means "a drying rack" for laundry. It is built from at tørre (to dry) and et stativ (a stand). Et stativ is any kind of stand or rack: et cykelstativ (a bike rack).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger tøjet på mit **tørrestativ**.
sentence.en: I hang the clothes on my drying rack.

tag det roligt.explanation: "Tag det roligt" means "take it easy" and "calm down". It is also a friendly goodbye: Ses i morgen, tag det roligt (See you tomorrow, take care).

forms.en: You have to take it easy

sentence.da: **Tag det roligt**, vi kommer ikke for sent.
sentence.en: Take it easy, we will not be late.

tak.explanation: "Tak" means "thanks", and Danish also uses it for "please": ja tak means "yes, please" and "Kaffe, tak" means "Coffee, please". You reply to thanks with selv tak (you're welcome).

sentence.da: **Tak** for maden!
sentence.en: Thanks for the food!

tak for det.explanation: "Tak for det" means "thanks for that", a friendly way to thank someone for something that just happened, like advice, help or a small favor. It is more casual than mange tak (thank you very much). You can put other words after tak for: Tak for kaffen means "Thanks for the coffee".

sentence.da: Her er din kaffe. **Tak for det**!
sentence.en: Here is your coffee. Thanks for that!

tak for i dag.explanation: "Tak for i dag" means "thanks for today", said when you part after a day together, such as work, a course or a meeting. Change i dag to i aften (tonight) for an evening, or say tak for sidst (thanks for last time) when you meet again.

forms.da: Tak for i dag, vi ses.

sentence.da: Vi ses i morgen. **Tak for i dag**!
sentence.en: See you tomorrow. Thanks for today!

tak for mad.explanation: "Tak for mad" means "thanks for the meal" (mad is food). You say it at the end of a meal to thank whoever made the food, and the reply is velbekomme (you're welcome, said about food).

forms.da: Tak for mad, det var lækkert.
forms.en: Thanks for the meal, it was delicious.

sentence.da: Maden var lækker. **Tak for mad**!
sentence.en: The food was delicious. Thanks for the meal!

tak for sidst.explanation: "Tak for sidst" means "thanks for last time" and is a friendly hello to someone you met before. Say it when you meet again, not when you leave.

forms.da: Tak for sidst, det var hyggeligt.
forms.en: Thanks for last time, that was nice.

sentence.da: **Tak for sidst**, det var en dejlig aften.
sentence.en: Thanks for last time, it was a lovely evening.

taknemmelig.explanation: "Taknemmelig" means "grateful". It is built from tak (thanks), and you add for to say what you are grateful for: Hun var taknemmelig for gaven (She was grateful for the gift).

sentence.da: Jeg er så **taknemmelig** for din hjælp.
sentence.en: I am so grateful for your help.

taknemmelighed.explanation: "Taknemmelighed" means "gratitude", the warm feeling of being thankful to someone for what they did. To say you feel it, use taknemmelig (grateful): Jeg er taknemmelig for hjælpen (I am grateful for the help).

sentence.da: Han sendte blomster som tegn på **taknemmelighed**.
sentence.en: He sent flowers as a sign of gratitude.

tal langsomt.explanation: "Tal langsomt" means "speak slowly". Adding tak (please) makes it polite, and Kan du tale langsommere? (Can you speak more slowly?) is even softer.

forms.da: Jeg forstår, når du taler langsomt
forms.en: I understand when you speak slowly

sentence.da: Jeg er ny her. **Tal langsomt**, tak.
sentence.en: I am new here. Speak slowly, please.

talentfuld.explanation: "Talentfuld" means "talented", naturally good at something such as music, sports or art. It is built from et talent (a talent) and -fuld (full of), the same -fuld as in meningsfuld (meaningful).

sentence.da: Han er en meget **talentfuld** fodboldspiller.
sentence.en: He is a very talented soccer player.

taler du engelsk?.explanation: "Taler du engelsk?" means "Do you speak English?". It is polite to try a little Danish first: Jeg taler lidt dansk (I speak a little Danish). To ask several people, say Taler I engelsk? (Do you all speak English?).

forms.en: I only speak a little Danish.

sentence.da: Undskyld, **taler du engelsk?**
sentence.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

tandpasta.explanation: "Tandpasta" means "toothpaste", the paste you put on a toothbrush to clean your teeth. You usually count it in tubes: to tuber tandpasta (two tubes of toothpaste).

sentence.da: Der er ikke mere **tandpasta** i tuben.
sentence.en: There is no more toothpaste in the tube.

tandpine.explanation: "Tandpine" means "toothache". It is built from tand (tooth) and pine (pain). You can also say Jeg har ondt i tanden (literally, I have pain in the tooth).

sentence.da: Jeg har **tandpine** og skal til tandlægen.
sentence.en: I have a toothache and need to go to the dentist.

tandtråd.explanation: "Tandtråd" means "dental floss", a thin thread you pull between your teeth to remove food. It is a joined word: tand (tooth) and tråd (thread).

sentence.da: Efter maden bruger jeg **tandtråd** mellem tænderne.
sentence.en: After the meal I use dental floss between my teeth.

tankefuld.explanation: "Tankefuld" means "pensive", about someone who is quiet and deep in thought, often with a faraway look. For "thoughtful" in the sense of kind and considerate, use omtenksom instead.

sentence.da: Han blev **tankefuld** og stirrede længe ud af vinduet.
sentence.en: He became pensive and stared out of the window for a long time.

tankeløs.explanation: "Tankeløs" means "thoughtless", acting without thinking about how it affects others. The ending -løs means "without", as in hjemløs (homeless).

sentence.da: Han er **tankeløs** og tænker aldrig på andre.
sentence.en: He is thoughtless and never thinks about others.

tape.explanation: "Tape" means "tape" for sticking things together, such as paper and packages.

sentence.da: Jeg klistrer plakaten op med **tape**.
sentence.en: I stick the poster up with tape.

tapet.explanation: "Tapet" means "wallpaper", the paper you put on a wall instead of paint.

sentence.da: Der er gammelt **tapet** på væggen.
sentence.en: There is old wallpaper on the wall.

tatoveret.explanation: "Tatoveret" means "tattooed", having a picture or text drawn permanently into the skin. It comes from at tatovere (to tattoo).

sentence.da: Hans arm er **tatoveret** med en stor drage.
sentence.en: His arm is tattooed with a big dragon.

tavs.explanation: "Tavs" means "silent", saying nothing, so it is about a person who does not speak. For a calm place without noise, use stille (quiet): et stille rum (a quiet room).

sentence.da: Hun var **tavs** og sagde ikke et ord.
sentence.en: She was silent and did not say a word.

te.explanation: "Te" means "tea". It is said like English tay, not like tee. Do not mix it up with ti (ten), which is said like tee.

sentence.da: Jeg drikker varm **te** med citron.
sentence.en: I drink hot tea with lemon.

tegnsætning.explanation: "Tegnsætning" means "punctuation", the marks in writing such as komma (comma) and punktum (period). It is built from tegn (mark) and at sætte (to put).

sentence.da: God **tegnsætning** gør det lettere at læse en tekst.
sentence.en: Good punctuation makes it easier to read a text.

teknisk.explanation: "Teknisk" means "technical", for machines, methods and how things work: Teknisk set er det muligt (Technically, it is possible).

sentence.da: Der er en **teknisk** fejl i systemet.
sentence.en: There is a technical error in the system.

temmelig.explanation: "Temmelig" means "rather" and "fairly". It is stronger than lidt (a little) but weaker than meget (very): lidt dyrt, temmelig dyrt, meget dyrt (a little expensive, rather expensive, very expensive).

sentence.da: Vejret er **temmelig** koldt for juni.
sentence.en: The weather is rather cold for June.

tennis.explanation: "Tennis" means "tennis". It goes with at spille (to play): Hun spiller tennis hver torsdag (She plays tennis every Thursday).

sentence.da: I **tennis** slår man bolden over nettet.
sentence.en: In tennis, you hit the ball over the net.

teoretisk.explanation: "Teoretisk" means "theoretical", about ideas and rules instead of real practice. Teoretisk set kan det lade sig gøre (Theoretically, it can be done) says something is possible in principle.

sentence.da: Bogen er **teoretisk** og forklarer ideer uden eksempler.
sentence.en: The book is theoretical and explains ideas without examples.

terapi.explanation: "Terapi" means "therapy", help for problems of the mind or body, most often regular talks with a trained person.

sentence.da: Hun går i **terapi** hver uge.
sentence.en: She goes to therapy every week.

ternet.explanation: "Ternet" means "checkered" or "plaid", with a pattern of squares. It is linked to en terning (a die), which also has square sides. Ternet papir (squared paper) is what Danes use in math.

sentence.da: Dugen på bordet er rød og hvid og **ternet**.
sentence.en: The cloth on the table is red and white and checkered.

terrorisme.explanation: "Terrorisme" means "terrorism", the use of violence or threats to frighten people for a political goal.

sentence.da: Mange lande samarbejder om at bekæmpe **terrorisme**.
sentence.en: Many countries work together to fight terrorism.

ti.explanation: "Ti" means "ten", said like tee. Do not mix it up with tid (time), which has a d on the end and sounds different.

sentence.da: Efter ni kommer **ti**.
sentence.en: After nine comes ten.

tidevand.explanation: "Et tidevand" means "a tide", the regular rising and falling of the sea. High water is højvande, and low water is lavvande. At the North Sea the tide is strong, but in the Baltic Sea it is hardly noticeable.

sentence.da: Når vandet går ud og kommer ind igen, kalder vi det **tidevand**.
sentence.en: When the water goes out and comes in again, we call that the tide.

tidlig.explanation: "Tidlig" means "early". To say you do something early, Danish uses tidligt: Jeg står tidligt op (I get up early).

sentence.da: Klokken fem om morgenen er meget **tidlig**.
sentence.en: Five o'clock in the morning is very early.

tidligere.explanation: "Tidligere" means "earlier" and also "former". For time, it means before now: Vi sås tidligere (We met earlier). Before a person or job, it means "former": en tidligere elev (a former student).

sentence.da: Hun har **tidligere** boet i Aarhus.
sentence.en: She has previously lived in Aarhus.

tidligt.explanation: "Tidligt" means "early". Compare Jeg står tidligt op (I get up early) with en tidlig morgen (an early morning): tidligt says when you do something, tidlig goes before a thing like morgen.

sentence.da: Jeg står **tidligt** op klokken fem.
sentence.en: I get up early at five o'clock.

tidskrævende.explanation: "Tidskrævende" means "time-consuming", taking a lot of time and effort. It is built from tid (time) and krævende (demanding): something that demands time.

sentence.da: Det er **tidskrævende** at skrive en lang rapport.
sentence.en: It is time-consuming to write a long report.

tidspres.explanation: "Tidspres" means "time pressure", having too little time before something must be finished. It is built from tid (time) and et pres (a pressure).

sentence.da: Det blev ikke færdigt på grund af **tidspres**.
sentence.en: It was not finished because of time pressure.

tidssvarende.explanation: "Tidssvarende" means "up to date", for things that fit the standards of the present, such as equipment, rules and buildings. For information that is current, use opdateret (updated) instead.

sentence.da: Reglerne er gamle og ikke længere **tidssvarende**.
sentence.en: The rules are old and no longer up to date.

tiende.explanation: "Tiende" means "tenth". It is used for dates: den tiende juni is the tenth of June, written 10. juni with a dot after the number.

sentence.da: Efter den niende kommer den **tiende**.
sentence.en: After the ninth comes the tenth.

til.explanation: "Til" means "to". Compare Jeg rejser til Danmark (I am traveling to Denmark) with Gaven er til dig (The gift is for you). It also fits meals and holidays: til morgenmad (for breakfast), til jul (at Christmas).

sentence.da: Jeg rejser **til** Aarhus i morgen.
sentence.en: I am traveling to Aarhus tomorrow.

til fælles.explanation: "Til fælles" means "in common" and usually follows at have (to have). It names what links people, like a hobby or a hometown.

forms.en: What do you have in common?

sentence.da: Vi har mange ting **til fælles**.
sentence.en: We have many things in common.

til gengæld.explanation: "Til gengæld" means "on the other hand", adding a good side to something bad. It also means "in return": Jeg laver mad, og til gengæld tager du opvasken (I cook, and in return you do the dishes).

forms.da: Det er dyrt, men til gengæld godt
forms.en: It is expensive, but on the other hand good

forms.da: Bilen er gammel, men til gengæld billig
forms.en: The car is old, but on the other hand cheap

sentence.da: Lejligheden er lille, men **til gengæld** ligger den centralt.
sentence.en: The apartment is small, but on the other hand it is centrally located.

til højre.explanation: "Til højre" means "to the right" or "on the right". The same phrase works for a direction and for where something is.

forms.en: The bank is on the right.

sentence.da: Min skole ligger **til højre** for kirken.
sentence.en: My school is to the right of the church.

til sidst.explanation: "Til sidst" means "finally" or "in the end", the last step after other things.

forms.en: In the end we went home

sentence.da: Vi spiste middag, og **til sidst** drak vi kaffe.
sentence.en: We had dinner, and finally we drank coffee.

til tiden.explanation: "Til tiden" means "on time", at the agreed time. It is not early and not late.

sentence.da: Bussen kom **til tiden**, og vi kom ikke for sent.
sentence.en: The bus came on time, and we were not late.

til venstre.explanation: "Til venstre" means "to the left" or "on the left". The same phrase works for a direction and for where something is.

forms.en: The post office is on the left.

sentence.da: Hjertet sidder **til venstre** i brystet.
sentence.en: The heart is on the left in the chest.

tilbage.explanation: "Tilbage" means "back" or "left over". Compare Hun går tilbage (She goes back) with Der er to tilbage (There are two left). For the back of your body, use ryg (back) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg kommer snart **tilbage**.
sentence.en: I will be back soon.

tilfreds.explanation: "Tilfreds" means "satisfied" or "content", for being fine with how something turned out.

sentence.da: Kunden er **tilfreds** med maden.
sentence.en: The customer is satisfied with the food.

tilfreds med.explanation: "Tilfreds med" means "satisfied with". The opposite is utilfreds med (unhappy with): Kunden er utilfreds med servicen (The customer is unhappy with the service).

forms.da: Jeg er tilfreds med min lejlighed.
forms.en: I am satisfied with my apartment.
Are you satisfied with the food?
We are satisfied with the house.

sentence.da: Jeg er **tilfreds med** mit nye job.
sentence.en: I am satisfied with my new job.

tilfredshed.explanation: "Tilfredshed" means "satisfaction", the content feeling that something is as good as you wanted. You often meet it in surveys: kundetilfredshed (customer satisfaction).

sentence.da: Hun så på sit arbejde med **tilfredshed**.
sentence.en: She looked at her work with satisfaction.

tilfredsstillende.explanation: "Tilfredsstillende" means "satisfying" or "satisfactory", good enough to meet what someone needs or expects. It comes from at tilfredsstille (to satisfy).

sentence.da: Resultatet var **tilfredsstillende**, og alle var glade.
sentence.en: The result was satisfactory, and everyone was happy.

tilfældig.explanation: "Tilfældig" means "random" and "by chance": et tilfældigt møde (a chance meeting). To say something happened by accident, use tilfældigvis: Jeg mødte ham tilfældigvis (I happened to meet him).

sentence.da: Jeg valgte en **tilfældig** bog fra hylden.
sentence.en: I chose a random book from the shelf.

tilfældigt.explanation: "Tilfældigt" means "randomly" or "by chance", without a plan or pattern, often about how you pick something. In a polite question like "Do you happen to have…", Danes use tilfældigvis instead.

sentence.da: Computeren vælger vinderen **tilfældigt** blandt alle deltagerne.
sentence.en: The computer picks the winner randomly among all the participants.

tilfældigvis.explanation: "Tilfældigvis" means "by chance" or "as it happens". In questions it makes a request polite: Har du tilfældigvis en kuglepen? (Do you happen to have a pen?).

forms.en: Do you happen to know her?

sentence.da: Jeg mødte **tilfældigvis** en gammel ven i byen.
sentence.en: I happened to meet an old friend in town.

tilgivelig.explanation: "Tilgivelig" means "forgivable", about a mistake or an act that someone can excuse. Its opposite is utilgivelig (unforgivable), which is the more common of the two.

sentence.da: Det var en **tilgivelig** fejl, fordi han var ny på arbejdet.
sentence.en: It was a forgivable mistake because he was new at work.

tilgivelse.explanation: "Tilgivelse" means "forgiveness", letting go of anger toward someone who has hurt you. It comes from at tilgive (to forgive).

sentence.da: Han bad om **tilgivelse**, fordi han havde løjet.
sentence.en: He asked for forgiveness because he had lied.

tilgængelig.explanation: "Tilgængelig" means "available" or "accessible", possible to reach, find or use. It is used for people (Er du tilgængelig? Are you available?), for things, and for buildings that wheelchair users can enter.

sentence.da: Informationen er **tilgængelig** for alle på nettet.
sentence.en: The information is available to everyone online.

tillid.explanation: "Tillid" means "trust", the belief that someone is honest and will not let you down. You can also say at stole på (to rely on): Jeg stoler på dig (I trust you).

sentence.da: Jeg har stor **tillid** til min læge.
sentence.en: I have great trust in my doctor.

tillidsfuld.explanation: "Tillidsfuld" means "trusting", about someone who expects others to be honest and kind. It is built from tillid (trust) and fuld (full), so it is literally "full of trust".

sentence.da: Den lille dreng så **tillidsfuld** op på sin far.
sentence.en: The little boy looked up trustingly at his father.

tillykke.explanation: "Tillykke" means "congratulations". Add med (on) and what you are celebrating: tillykke med bilen (congratulations on the car).

sentence.da: **Tillykke** med din nye lejlighed!
sentence.en: Congratulations on your new apartment!

tillykke med fødselsdagen.explanation: "Tillykke med fødselsdagen" means "happy birthday", literally, congratulations with the birthday. It can be shortened to tillykke med dagen (congratulations on the day).

sentence.da: Her er en gave. **Tillykke med fødselsdagen**!
sentence.en: Here is a present. Happy birthday!

tilmed.explanation: "Tilmed" means "moreover", adding one more point that makes the case stronger. It sounds more written than spoken; in speech Danes often say oven i købet (on top of that).

forms.da: Det er billigt og tilmed godt
forms.en: It is cheap and moreover good

forms.da: Han er klog, og tilmed er han flink
forms.en: He is smart, and moreover he is kind

forms.da: Maden er sund og tilmed lækker
forms.en: The food is healthy and moreover delicious

sentence.da: Cyklen er billig, og den er **tilmed** let at reparere.
sentence.en: The bike is cheap, and it is moreover easy to repair.

tilpas.explanation: "Tilpas" means "just right" or "suitable": Suppen er tilpas varm (The soup is warm enough). With at føle sig (to feel), it means "at ease": Jeg føler mig ikke tilpas (I do not feel at ease).

sentence.da: Vandet er **tilpas** varmt til at bade.
sentence.en: The water is just warm enough for swimming.

tilsammen.explanation: "Tilsammen" means "in total" and also "together": Vi betaler 300 kroner tilsammen (We pay 300 kroner in total). Use sammen (together) when people do something with each other: Vi spiser sammen (We eat together).

forms.en: It is ten kroner in total
There are five of us in total

sentence.da: Vi er ti personer **tilsammen**.
sentence.en: We are ten people in total.

tilstedeværelse.explanation: "En tilstedeværelse" means "a presence", the fact that someone or something is there. It is built from til stede (present) and at være (to be), and its opposite is fravær (absence).

sentence.da: Lærerens **tilstedeværelse** i klassen gør børnene mere rolige.
sentence.en: The teacher's presence in the class makes the children calmer.

tilstrækkelig.explanation: "Tilstrækkelig" means "sufficient", as much as is needed and no more. It is linked to at strække til (to be enough), as in Pengene strækker ikke til (The money is not enough).

sentence.da: Fem timers søvn er ikke **tilstrækkelig** for de fleste.
sentence.en: Five hours of sleep is not sufficient for most people.

tilsyneladende.explanation: "Tilsyneladende" means "apparently", based on how things look, which may turn out to be wrong. For something you only heard from others, use efter sigende (reportedly).

sentence.da: Butikken er **tilsyneladende** lukket i dag.
sentence.en: The store is apparently closed today.

tiltro.explanation: "En tiltro" means "confidence" or "trust", a belief that someone or something is good and will work. It almost always comes with til (in): have tiltro til dig (have confidence in you).

forms.en: to have confidence in the system

sentence.da: Efter skandalen mistede folk al **tiltro** til politikerne.
sentence.en: After the scandal people lost all confidence in the politicians.

tiltrukket.explanation: "Tiltrukket" means "attracted", pulled toward someone or something by a feeling. It is almost always followed by af (by), as in tiltrukket af hende (attracted to her).

forms.en: We are drawn to the city

sentence.da: Bierne er **tiltrukket** af blomsternes søde duft.
sentence.en: The bees are attracted to the sweet scent of the flowers.

tiltrækkende.explanation: "Tiltrækkende" means "attractive", pulling people toward it, for a person, an offer or a place. The one that pulls is tiltrækkende, and the one who feels pulled is tiltrukket (attracted): Han er tiltrukket af hende, for hun er tiltrækkende (He is attracted to her, because she is attractive).

sentence.da: Prisen gør tilbuddet meget **tiltrækkende**.
sentence.en: The price makes the offer very attractive.

timevis.explanation: "Timevis" means "for hours", a long time counted in hours. The ending -vis does the same with other times: dagevis (for days).

sentence.da: Jeg kan sidde **timevis** med en god bog.
sentence.en: I can sit for hours with a good book.

tirsdag.explanation: "Tirsdag" means "Tuesday". Day names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish. På tirsdag means on Tuesday (the coming one), and om tirsdagen or hver tirsdag means every Tuesday.

sentence.da: Efter mandag kommer **tirsdag**.
sentence.en: After Monday comes Tuesday.

tja.explanation: "Tja" means "well" and shows that you are unsure or thinking: Kommer du? Tja, måske (Are you coming? Well, maybe). It is a short sound you say before an answer.

sentence.da: **Tja**, jeg ved ikke helt, hvad jeg skal sige.
sentence.en: Well, I do not quite know what to say.

to.explanation: "To" means "two". It stays the same before any word. In numbers like 22 the ones come first: toogtyve (twenty-two) is literally two-and-twenty.

sentence.da: En, **to**, tre!
sentence.en: One, two, three!

to gange.explanation: "To gange" means "twice", literally two times. Add om dagen, om ugen or om måneden to say how often: to gange om ugen (twice a week).

sentence.da: Én gang, **to gange**, tre gange!
sentence.en: Once, twice, three times!

tofu.explanation: "Tofu" means "tofu", a soft white block made from beans that has little taste of its own, so it takes on the flavor of the sauce or spices.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **tofu** i stedet for kød.
sentence.en: I would like tofu instead of meat.

toiletpapir.explanation: "Toiletpapir" means "toilet paper", the soft paper on a roll that you use in the bathroom. You count it in rolls: en rulle (one roll), to ruller (two rolls).

sentence.da: Man bruger **toiletpapir** på toilettet.
sentence.en: You use toilet paper in the bathroom.

told.explanation: "Told" means "customs", the place at a border or airport where goods are checked. It also means a tax on goods from abroad: Man skal betale told (You have to pay duty).

sentence.da: Der er lang kø ved **told** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: There is a long line at customs at the airport.

tolerant.explanation: "Tolerant" means "tolerant", open to people who think, believe or live differently than you do. The opposite is intolerant (intolerant), which Danish spells the same way.

sentence.da: Et **tolerant** samfund giver plads til alle slags mennesker.
sentence.en: A tolerant society makes room for all kinds of people.

tolv.explanation: "Tolv" means "twelve". For twelve of something, Danes also say et dusin (a dozen): et dusin æg (a dozen eggs).

sentence.da: Efter elleve kommer **tolv**.
sentence.en: After eleven comes twelve.

tolvte.explanation: "Tolvte" means "twelfth", the place number for 12 in a row, and it is used for dates: Min fødselsdag er den tolvte (My birthday is on the twelfth).

sentence.da: Dagen efter den ellevte er den **tolvte**.
sentence.en: The day after the eleventh is the twelfth.

tom.explanation: "Tom" means "empty", for a bottle, a room, a street or a plate. The opposite is fuld (full), which can also mean "drunk" when it describes a person.

sentence.da: Der er intet vand. Flasken er **tom**.
sentence.en: There is no water. The bottle is empty.

tomhændet.explanation: "Tomhændet" means "empty-handed", with nothing to bring, such as no gift for a party, or with nothing to show for your effort.

sentence.da: Hun købte blomster, fordi hun ikke ville komme **tomhændet**.
sentence.en: She bought flowers because she did not want to come empty-handed.

torden.explanation: "Torden" means "thunder", the loud sound in a storm. Say Det tordner (It is thundering) for what is happening now.

sentence.da: Efter lyn kommer **torden**.
sentence.en: After lightning comes thunder.

torsdag.explanation: "Torsdag" means "Thursday". Day names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish. På torsdag means on Thursday (the coming one), and "om torsdagen" means "on Thursdays". Do not mix it up with tirsdag (Tuesday), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Efter onsdag kommer **torsdag**.
sentence.en: After Wednesday comes Thursday.

torsk.explanation: "Torsk" means "cod", both the fish in the sea and the fish on your plate. For the animal, say en torsk (a cod). For the food just say torsk: Vi spiser torsk (We eat cod).

sentence.da: Fiskeren fanger en stor **torsk** i havet.
sentence.en: The fisherman catches a big cod in the sea.

tortur.explanation: "En tortur" means "torture", severe pain or suffering that someone causes on purpose. In daily talk it also describes something very unpleasant: Det var en tortur at vente (Waiting was torture).

sentence.da: **Tortur** er at gøre ondt på et menneske med vilje.
sentence.en: Torture is hurting a person on purpose.

tosproget.explanation: "Tosproget" means "bilingual", able to speak two languages well. It also describes things that use two languages, such as et tosproget skilt (a bilingual sign).

sentence.da: Hun er **tosproget** og taler både dansk og engelsk hjemme.
sentence.en: She is bilingual and speaks both Danish and English at home.

tosset.explanation: "Tosset" means "silly" or "crazy", in a light and friendly way: Du er tosset! (You are silly!). It is much milder than sindssyg (insane).

sentence.da: Han er **tosset**, men ikke farlig.
sentence.en: He is silly, but not dangerous.

total.explanation: "Total" means "total", with nothing left out. The word totalt (totally) makes another word stronger: Jeg er totalt træt (I am totally tired).

sentence.da: Det var en **total** katastrofe, og alle var kede af det.
sentence.en: It was a total disaster, and everyone was upset about it.

totalt.explanation: "Totalt" means "totally" and makes the next word stronger. It is a bit more emphatic than helt (all the way), which you can use in the same places.

sentence.da: Jeg er **totalt** træt efter turen.
sentence.en: I am totally tired after the trip.

traditionel.explanation: "Traditionel" means "traditional", for customs, food and ways of doing things. The opposite is moderne (modern).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **traditionel** mad til jul.
sentence.en: We eat traditional food at Christmas.

trafik.explanation: "Trafik" means "traffic" on the roads. A traffic jam is en trafikprop.

sentence.da: Der er meget **trafik** på motorvejen i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of traffic on the highway today.

tragisk.explanation: "Tragisk" means "tragic" and is used for terrible events, like accidents and losses. It is too strong for a small problem, like a missed bus.

sentence.da: Det var en **tragisk** dag, og alle græd.
sentence.en: It was a tragic day, and everyone cried.

trang.explanation: "Trang" means "cramped", with too little room, for places and for clothes alike. It is also used about money: at leve på trange kår means to live on very little.

sentence.da: I en **trang** lejlighed er der næsten ikke plads til møbler.
sentence.en: In a cramped apartment there is hardly room for furniture.

travl.explanation: "Travl" means "busy", for a person, a day, a street or a shop. Jeg har det travlt means "I am busy" or "I am in a hurry".

sentence.da: Jeg har meget at lave. Jeg er **travl**.
sentence.en: I have a lot to do. I am busy.

tre.explanation: "Tre" means "three". It stays the same before any word.

sentence.da: Efter to kommer **tre**.
sentence.en: After two comes three.

tredive.explanation: "Tredive" means "thirty". In 31, the one comes first: enogtredive (thirty-one) is literally one-and-thirty.

sentence.da: Tyve, **tredive**, fyrre.
sentence.en: Twenty, thirty, forty.

tredje.explanation: "Tredje" means "third". It is used for dates too: den tredje oktober is the third of October.

sentence.da: Den første, den anden og den **tredje**.
sentence.en: The first, the second and the third.

tres.explanation: "Tres" means "sixty". Do not mix it up with tre (three) or tredive (thirty): tre børn (three children), tres børn (sixty children).

sentence.da: Halvtreds, **tres**, halvfjerds.
sentence.en: Fifty, sixty, seventy.

tretten.explanation: "Tretten" means "thirteen". It stays the same before any word.

sentence.da: Tolv, **tretten**, fjorten.
sentence.en: Twelve, thirteen, fourteen.

trist.explanation: "Trist" means "sad". It describes a person who feels sad, and also things that are sad or dull, such as a film or gray weather.

sentence.da: Hun er **trist** og græder.
sentence.en: She is sad and crying.

trivsel.explanation: "En trivsel" means "well-being", how comfortable and happy someone feels in a place such as a school or a job. It comes from the verb at trives (to thrive, to feel at home).

sentence.da: Skolen arbejder for børnenes **trivsel**, så ingen skal føle sig alene.
sentence.en: The school works for the children's well-being, so that no one feels alone.

tro.explanation: "Tro" means "faith" or "belief": Hun mister aldrig sin tro (She never loses her faith). The same word is also at tro (to think, to believe): Jeg tror, det er rigtigt (I think it is right).

sentence.da: Hendes **tro** på Gud giver hende ro.
sentence.en: Her faith in God gives her peace.

trods.explanation: "Trods" means "despite" and is followed by whatever was in the way: trods regnen (despite the rain). The longer på trods af means the same.

sentence.da: **Trods** den høje pris købte hun den dyre jakke.
sentence.en: Despite the high price, she bought the expensive jacket.

trods alt.explanation: "Trods alt" means "after all", used when something turns out good or true even though there were problems on the way. Literally it is "despite everything".

forms.en: She got the job after all.

sentence.da: Der var mange problemer, men vi nåede **trods alt** frem.
sentence.en: There were many problems, but we got there after all.

troende.explanation: "Troende" means "believing" or "religious", about someone who has a faith: en troende muslim (a believing Muslim). Used alone it names such people: de troende (the believers). It comes from at tro (to believe).

sentence.da: Hun er en **troende** kvinde og går i kirke hver søndag.
sentence.en: She is a religious woman and goes to church every Sunday.

trofast.explanation: "Trofast" means "faithful", staying loyal over a long time, for example a friend, a dog or a partner. It is built from tro (loyal, true) and fast (firm).

sentence.da: Min hund er en **trofast** ven, som venter ved døren.
sentence.en: My dog is a faithful friend who waits at the door.

troskab.explanation: "En troskab" means "loyalty", staying faithful to a person, a promise or a country. In a relationship it means being faithful to your partner, and its opposite is utroskab (infidelity).

sentence.da: Soldaten svor **troskab** mod kongen.
sentence.en: The soldier swore loyalty to the king.

trusser.explanation: "Trusser" means "panties" or "briefs", women's underwear, and it is normally used in the plural. For men's underwear, use underbukser (underpants); undertøj (underwear) covers underwear in general.

sentence.da: Hun tager **trusser** og bukser på.
sentence.en: She puts on panties and pants.

tryg.explanation: "Tryg" means "safe" or "secure", the calm feeling of being looked after: Børnene er trygge hos deres bedstemor (The children feel safe with their grandmother). The opposite is utryg (uneasy).

sentence.da: Jeg føler mig **tryg** sammen med dig.
sentence.en: I feel safe with you.

tryghed.explanation: "Tryghed" means "security" or "safety", the calm feeling that nothing bad will happen: Hun giver mig tryghed (She gives me security).

sentence.da: Børn har brug for **tryghed** hjemme.
sentence.en: Children need security at home.

trygt.explanation: "Trygt" means "safely", with no risk or worry. In Du kan trygt spørge (You can safely ask), it means "feel free to": you have nothing to fear.

forms.en: You can move about safely here.

sentence.da: Børn skal kunne lege **trygt** i deres eget kvarter.
sentence.en: Children should be able to play safely in their own neighborhood.

trådløs.explanation: "Trådløs" means "wireless". It is built from tråd (wire) and the ending -løs (-less), so it describes things that work without being plugged in.

sentence.da: Min nye højttaler er **trådløs** og har ikke noget kabel.
sentence.en: My new speaker is wireless and has no cable.

træg.explanation: "Træg" means "sluggish", taking a long time to get going, with little energy. It is used for a person, a body or a computer.

sentence.da: Trafikken var **træg**, fordi der var mange biler.
sentence.en: The traffic was sluggish because there were many cars.

træning.explanation: "Træning" means "training / exercise", the work you do to get fitter or better: Jeg har træning i aften (I have training tonight). It is also the word for team practice: Fodboldtræning er klokken seks (Soccer practice is at six).

sentence.da: Efter **træning** er jeg altid sulten og træt.
sentence.en: After training I am always hungry and tired.

træningstøj.explanation: "Træningstøj" means "workout clothes", the clothes you wear for sport. It covers the whole outfit, so you do not make a plural.

sentence.da: Jeg har **træningstøj** på, når jeg løber.
sentence.en: I wear workout clothes when I run.

træt.explanation: "Træt" means "tired". With af (of), it means "fed up with": træt af det (fed up with it).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **træt** og vil sove.
sentence.en: I am very tired and want to sleep.

træt af.explanation: "Træt af" means "tired of" or "fed up with", when you have had enough: Jeg er træt af støjen (I am fed up with the noise). Without af, Jeg er træt (I am tired) is about sleep.

sentence.da: Jeg er **træt af** at vente her.
sentence.en: I am tired of waiting here.

træthed.explanation: "En træthed" means "tiredness", the feeling of having no energy and needing rest. It names the state itself; to say that you are tired, you use træt.

sentence.da: Manglende søvn giver **træthed** og dårlig koncentration.
sentence.en: Lack of sleep causes tiredness and poor concentration.

trøst.explanation: "Trøst" means "comfort" or "consolation", what you give someone who is sad: Barnet fik trøst hos sin mor (The child got comfort from her mother). Det er en lille trøst means "That is a small comfort".

sentence.da: Hun fandt **trøst** hos sine venner.
sentence.en: She found comfort with her friends.

tun.explanation: "Tun" means "tuna", both the fish and the canned kind. Tuna with mayonnaise is called tunsalat (tuna salad).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg **tun** med salat.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat tuna with salad.

tung.explanation: "Tung" means "heavy", for a bag, a box or shopping. It also describes food that feels heavy in the stomach: tung mad (heavy food).

sentence.da: Tasken er meget **tung** at løfte.
sentence.en: The bag is very heavy to lift.

turkis.explanation: "Turkis" means "turquoise", a blue-green color. Note the spelling: Danish has a k where English has qu.

sentence.da: Blå og grøn bliver **turkis**.
sentence.en: Blue and green make turquoise.

tusind.explanation: "Tusind" means "a thousand". Fem tusind is five thousand. Years are said with hundreds instead: 1999 is nitten hundrede og nioghalvfems (nineteen hundred and ninety-nine).

sentence.da: Ti gange hundrede er **tusind**.
sentence.en: Ten times a hundred is a thousand.

tusind tak.explanation: "Tusind tak" means "thanks a lot", literally a thousand thanks. It is a little warmer than mange tak (thank you very much). Use it when someone has really helped you.

forms.en: Thanks a lot for your help.

forms.da: Tusind tak, det var pænt af dig.
forms.en: Thanks a lot, that was kind of you.

sentence.da: Du har hjulpet mig så meget. **Tusind tak**!
sentence.en: You have helped me so much. Thanks a lot!

tusindvis.explanation: "Tusindvis" means "thousands" and is followed by af and the thing counted. It gives a rough size, many thousands, not an exact number.

sentence.da: Ved en stor koncert er der **tusindvis** af mennesker.
sentence.en: At a big concert there are thousands of people.

tvetydig.explanation: "Tvetydig" means "ambiguous", a sentence, answer or hint that can be understood in two different ways. The start tve- means two, as in tvilling (twin).

sentence.da: Det er en **tvetydig** sætning, for den kan forstås på to måder.
sentence.en: It is an ambiguous sentence, because it can be understood in two ways.

tvivlsom.explanation: "Tvivlsom" means "doubtful", not certain to be true, good or honest, so you do not fully trust it. It describes the thing, while a person who feels unsure is usikker (unsure).

sentence.da: Jeg synes, hans forklaring er meget **tvivlsom**.
sentence.en: I think his explanation is very doubtful.

tvungen.explanation: "Tvungen" means "forced", done because a rule or a situation leaves you no choice, not because you want to. It comes from at tvinge (to force).

sentence.da: Det var ikke et frit valg, men en **tvungen** løsning.
sentence.en: It was not a free choice but a forced solution.

tværtimod.explanation: "Tværtimod" means "on the contrary", used to answer a statement by saying that the opposite is true: Generer jeg dig? Tværtimod! (Am I bothering you? On the contrary!)

forms.en: It is not expensive, on the contrary.
On the contrary, it was a pleasure.

sentence.da: Han er ikke doven, **tværtimod** arbejder han meget.
sentence.en: He is not lazy, on the contrary he works a lot.

tydelig.explanation: "Tydelig" means "clear" in the sense of easy to see or understand. Tal tydeligt (Speak clearly). For clear water or clear skies, use klar (clear).

sentence.da: Hendes stemme er **tydelig**, så alle kan høre hende.
sentence.en: Her voice is clear, so everyone can hear her.

tydeligvis.explanation: "Tydeligvis" means "obviously", used when the signs show that something is true, even if nobody has said it. It is not the same as selvfølgelig (of course), which says something goes without saying.

sentence.da: Han er **tydeligvis** hjemme, fordi der er lys i vinduet.
sentence.en: He is obviously home because there is a light in the window.

tyggegummi.explanation: "Tyggegummi" means "chewing gum". It is built from at tygge (to chew) and gummi (rubber). Gummi on its own means rubber, as in gummistøvler (rubber boots).

sentence.da: Børnene tygger **tyggegummi** og blæser store bobler.
sentence.en: The kids chew chewing gum and blow big bubbles.

tyk.explanation: "Tyk" means "thick", such as a thick coat. About a person it means "fat", and it is as blunt as that word in English, so avoid it.

sentence.da: Bogen har mange sider. Den er **tyk**.
sentence.en: The book has many pages. It is thick.

tynd.explanation: "Tynd" means "thin", for a book, a layer, a slice or a piece of cloth. It also describes watery liquids, such as tynd suppe (thin soup). About a person it can sound negative; slank (slim) is the kinder word.

sentence.da: Bogen har få sider. Den er **tynd**.
sentence.en: The book has few pages. It is thin.

tyngdekraft.explanation: "En tyngdekraft" means "gravity", the force that pulls things down toward the earth. Literally it is "weight force", from tyngde (weight) and kraft (force).

sentence.da: Uden **tyngdekraft** ville tingene svæve rundt i luften.
sentence.en: Without gravity things would float around in the air.

typisk.explanation: "Typisk" means "typical": Det er typisk for ham (That is typical of him). Said alone, Typisk! means "Typical!" when something goes wrong again.

sentence.da: Det er en **typisk** dansk ret med kartofler.
sentence.en: It is a typical Danish dish with potatoes.

tyrkiet.explanation: "Tyrkiet" means "Turkey", the country. The bird is en kalkun (a turkey).

sentence.da: Istanbul er en stor by i **Tyrkiet**.
sentence.en: Istanbul is a big city in Turkey.

tyrkisk.explanation: "Tyrkisk" means "Turkish", for people, things and the language. It is written with a small letter, where English writes Turkish with a capital.

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Tyrkiet og taler **tyrkisk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Turkey and speaks Turkish.

tysk.explanation: "Tysk" means "German", for things from Germany and for the language. It is written with a small letter, where English writes German with a capital.

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Tyskland og taler **tysk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Germany and speaks German.

tyskland.explanation: "Tyskland" means "Germany". It is made of tysk (German) and land (country). Tysk is also the language: Jeg taler tysk (I speak German).

sentence.da: Berlin er en stor by i **Tyskland**.
sentence.en: Berlin is a big city in Germany.

tyve.explanation: "Tyve" means "twenty". In numbers like 21 the ones come first: enogtyve (twenty-one) is literally one-and-twenty, and 22 is toogtyve (twenty-two, literally two-and-twenty).

sentence.da: Ti og ti er **tyve**.
sentence.en: Ten and ten is twenty.

tyvende.explanation: "Tyvende" means "twentieth", the place number for 20 in a row. It is also how Danes say the century: det tyvende århundrede (the twentieth century).

sentence.da: Efter den nittende dag kommer den **tyvende**.
sentence.en: After the nineteenth day comes the twentieth.

tåbelig.explanation: "Tåbelig" means "foolish", for an idea, a remark or a decision that is silly and not well thought through. In everyday speech Danes more often say dum (stupid).

sentence.da: Det var en **tåbelig** idé at gå ud uden jakke.
sentence.en: It was a foolish idea to go out without a jacket.

tåge.explanation: "Tåge" means "fog". To say it is foggy, say Der er tåge (There is fog) or Det er tåget (It is foggy).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke se langt i **tåge**.
sentence.en: You cannot see far in fog.

tålmodig.explanation: "Tålmodig" means "patient", describing someone who does not get upset when things take time. The opposite is utålmodig (impatient).

related.en: to bear, to put up with

sentence.da: Hun er **tålmodig** og venter uden at klage.
sentence.en: She is patient and waits without complaining.

tålmodighed.explanation: "Tålmodighed" means "patience", not getting upset while you wait or learn. Someone who has it is tålmodig (patient): Vær tålmodig (Be patient).

sentence.da: Det kræver **tålmodighed** at lære et nyt sprog.
sentence.en: It takes patience to learn a new language.

tæt.explanation: "Tæt" means "close" and "tight", with no gaps. For places, it goes with på (on): Jeg bor tæt på skolen (I live close to the school). For things, it means nothing gets through, such as water.

sentence.da: Taget er **tæt**, og regnen kommer ikke ind.
sentence.en: The roof is tight, and the rain does not come in.

tæt på.explanation: "Tæt på" means "close to" and tells how close a place or person is. The opposite is langt fra (far from).

sentence.da: Hotellet ligger **tæt på** stranden.
sentence.en: The hotel is close to the beach.

tøj.explanation: "Tøj" means "clothes". It is one word for all your clothes together: mit tøj (my clothes), noget tøj (some clothes). One item has its own name, such as en trøje (a sweater).

sentence.da: Bukser og trøjer er **tøj**.
sentence.en: Trousers and sweaters are clothes.

tømmer.explanation: "Et tømmer" means "timber", wood from felled trees used for building, such as logs. Do not mix it up with tømmer from at tømme (to empty): Jeg tømmer skabet (I empty the cabinet).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **tømmer** fra skoven til at bygge huset.
sentence.en: We use timber from the forest to build the house.

tømmermænd.explanation: "Tømmermænd" means "a hangover", the sick, tired feeling the morning after too much alcohol. Danish uses it only in the plural, so you say Jeg har tømmermænd (I have a hangover).

sentence.da: Efter festen havde han **tømmermænd** og ville bare sove.
sentence.en: After the party he had a hangover and just wanted to sleep.

tør.explanation: "Tør" means "dry", for clothes, weather, skin or bread. Do not mix it up with tør in jeg tør ikke (I dare not): it is a different word that looks the same.

sentence.da: Jakken var våd. Nu er den **tør**.
sentence.en: The jacket was wet. Now it is dry.

tørret frugt.explanation: "Tørret frugt" means "dried fruit", fruit with the water taken out so it keeps for a long time and tastes sweet.

sentence.da: Rosiner og abrikoser er **tørret frugt**.
sentence.en: Raisins and apricots are dried fruit.

tørstig.explanation: "Tørstig" means "thirsty". Jeg er tørstig means "I am thirsty". Danes also say Jeg har tørst, literally I have thirst.

sentence.da: Jeg er **tørstig** og vil have vand.
sentence.en: I am thirsty and want water.
